sentences.zh: 【唐紀四十七】起閼逢困敦五月，盡旃蒙赤奮若七月，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Annals 47] From the fifth month of Eyu Kundun through the seventh month of Zhanmeng Chifenruo; a little more than one year in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Annals 47] From the fifth month of the Eyu Kundun cycle year through the seventh month of the Zhanmeng Chifenruo cycle year—a little more than one year in all.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝六興元元年（

translations.literal: Sixth year of Xingyuan of Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial and Sagely Literate Emperor (
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year of Xingyuan of Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial and Sagely Literate Emperor (

sentences.zh: 甲子，公元七八四年）

translations.literal: jiazi, AD 784)
translations.idiomatic: jiazi, A.D. 784)

sentences.zh: 五月，鹽鐵判官萬年王紹以江、淮繒帛來至，上命先給將士，然後御衫。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Wang Shao of Wannian, salt-and-iron commissioner, arrived with silk fabrics from the Jiang and Huai regions. The emperor ordered that the troops be supplied first and only afterward garments for himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Wang Shao of Wannian, the salt-and-iron commissioner, arrived with silk goods from the Jiang and Huai regions. The emperor ordered that the soldiers be clothed first and only then himself.

sentences.zh: 韓滉欲遣使獻綾羅四十擔詣行在，幕僚何士幹請行，滉喜曰：「君能相為行，請今日過江。」

translations.literal: Han Huang wished to send an envoy to present forty loads of damask and gauze to the imperial camp. His staff officer He Shigan volunteered to go. Huang said with pleasure, "If you can make the journey for me, please cross the river today."
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang wished to send an envoy bearing forty loads of damask and gauze to the imperial camp. His staff officer He Shigan volunteered for the mission. Huang said gladly, "If you will make the trip for me, cross the river today."

sentences.zh: 士幹許諾，歸別家，則家之薪米儲偫已羅門庭矣；

translations.literal: Shigan agreed. When he returned home to take leave of his family, firewood, rice, and provisions already filled the courtyard;
translations.idiomatic: Shigan agreed. When he went home to bid his family farewell, firewood, rice, and stores already filled the courtyard;

sentences.zh: 登舟，則資裝器用已充舟中矣。

translations.literal: when he boarded the boat, funds, baggage, and utensils already filled the vessel.
translations.idiomatic: and when he boarded the boat, funds, baggage, and utensils already filled it.

sentences.zh: 下至廁籌，滉皆手筆記列，無不周備。

translations.literal: Down to toilet reeds, Huang had listed everything in his own hand—nothing was left out.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the reeds for the privy, Huang had listed everything in his own hand—nothing was omitted.

sentences.zh: 每擔夫，與白金一版置腰間。

translations.literal: To each bearer he gave a plate of white gold to wear at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Each bearer received a plate of white gold to wear at his waist.

sentences.zh: 又運米百艘以餉李晟，自負囊米至舟中，將佐爭舉之，須臾而畢。

translations.literal: He also sent a hundred grain boats to supply Li Sheng. He himself carried sack-loads of rice aboard; his officers and aides vied to lift them, and the work was finished in no time.
translations.idiomatic: He also dispatched a hundred grain boats to supply Li Sheng. He carried sack-loads of rice aboard himself; his officers and aides rushed to help, and the loading was done in moments.

sentences.zh: 艘置五弩手以為防援，有寇則叩舷相警，五百弩已彀矣。

translations.literal: On each boat he placed five crossbowmen as escort; if raiders appeared they would rap the gunwales to warn one another—five hundred crossbows were already strung.
translations.idiomatic: Each boat carried five crossbowmen as escort; if raiders appeared they would rap the gunwales to alert the fleet—five hundred crossbows stood ready.

sentences.zh: 比至渭橋，資不敢近。

translations.literal: By the time they reached Weiqiao, Zi did not dare approach.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached Weiqiao, the rebel Zi did not dare come near.

sentences.zh: 時關中兵荒，米斗直錢五百，及滉米至，減五之四。

translations.literal: At the time Guanzhong was ravaged by war; a dou of rice cost five hundred cash. When Huang's grain arrived, the price fell by four-fifths.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong was then ravaged by war and a dou of rice sold for five hundred cash. When Huang's grain arrived, the price dropped by four-fifths.

sentences.zh: 滉為人強力嚴毅，自奉儉素，夫人常衣絹裙，破，然後易。

translations.literal: Huang was by nature forceful, strict, and resolute; he lived frugally himself. His wife commonly wore a silk skirt and changed it only after it was worn out.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was forceful, strict, and resolute by nature and lived frugally. His wife commonly wore a silk skirt and replaced it only after it was worn through.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃既破韓旻等，大掠而去。

translations.literal: The Tibetans, having defeated Han Min and the others, looted on a great scale and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Han Min and his fellows, the Tibetans plundered extensively and marched away.

sentences.zh: 朱泚使田希鑒厚以金帛賂之，吐蕃受之。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci sent Tian Xijian to bribe them lavishly with gold and silk, and the Tibetans accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci sent Tian Xijian to ply them with lavish gifts of gold and silk, and the Tibetans took them.

sentences.zh: 韓游瑰以聞。

translations.literal: Han Yougui reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui reported it to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 渾瑊又奏：「尚結贊屢遣人約刻日共取長安，既而不至。

translations.literal: Hun Jian also memorialized: "Shang Jiezan repeatedly sent men to agree on a fixed day to jointly take Chang'an, yet in the end did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian also submitted a memorial: "Shang Jiezan has repeatedly sent envoys to fix a date for a joint advance on Chang'an, yet each time he failed to appear.

sentences.zh: 聞其眾今春大疫，近已引兵去。」

translations.literal: It is heard that his troops suffered a great plague this spring and have recently withdrawn their army."
translations.idiomatic: Word has it that his troops were ravaged by plague this spring and have lately marched away."

sentences.zh: 上以李晟、渾瑊兵少，欲倚吐蕃以復京城，聞其去，甚憂之，以問陸贄。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Li Sheng and Hun Jian had few troops, wished to rely on the Tibetans to recover the capital; hearing they had departed, he was deeply worried and asked Lu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, finding Li Sheng and Hun Jian short of men, had hoped to lean on the Tibetans to retake the capital. When he heard they had left, he was deeply troubled and consulted Lu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 贄以為吐蕃貪狡，有害無益，得其引去，實可欣賀。

translations.literal: Zhi believed the Tibetans were greedy and cunning, harmful and of no benefit; that they had withdrawn was truly cause for rejoicing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi held that the Tibetans were greedy and treacherous—more harm than help—and that their departure was in truth grounds for celebration.

sentences.zh: 乃上奏，其略曰：「吐蕃遷延觀望，翻覆多端，深入郊畿，陰受賊使，致令群帥進退憂虞：欲捨之獨前，則慮其懷怨乘躡；

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial, in summary saying: "The Tibetans delay and wait to see, shifting course at every turn; they have penetrated deep into the capital outskirts and secretly receive rebel envoys, leaving the commanders anxious whether to advance or hold back: if one wishes to leave them and press on alone, one fears they will harbor resentment and strike from behind;
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized the throne, in substance saying: "The Tibetans stall and watch how matters fall, reversing themselves at every turn. They have pushed deep into the capital suburbs and secretly take envoys from the rebels, leaving our generals torn over whether to advance or hold back: go on without them and you fear they will nurse a grudge and strike at your rear;

sentences.zh: 欲待之合勢，則若其失信稽延。

translations.literal: if one wishes to wait for them to combine forces, it is as if they will break faith and drag out delays.
translations.idiomatic: wait for them to join in a combined drive and you risk broken promises and endless delay.

sentences.zh: 戎若未歸，寇終不滅。」

translations.literal: If the barbarians do not depart, the rebels will never be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: While the Tibetans remain, the rebels will never be crushed."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「將帥意陛下不見信任，且患蕃戎之奪其功；

translations.literal: He also said: "The commanders believe Your Majesty does not trust them and fear the barbarians will steal their credit;
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Your generals suspect they are not trusted and fear the Tibetans will steal the glory of their victory;

sentences.zh: 士卒恐陛下不恤舊勞，而畏蕃戎之專其利；

translations.literal: the soldiers fear Your Majesty will not care for their past labors and dread that the barbarians will monopolize the gains;
translations.idiomatic: the rank and file fear their past service will go unrewarded and that the Tibetans will keep all the spoils for themselves;

sentences.zh: 賊黨懼蕃戎之勝，不死則悉遺人禽；

translations.literal: the rebel band fear a Tibetan victory—if they are not killed they will all be handed over and captured;
translations.idiomatic: the rebels dread a Tibetan triumph—if they are not killed outright they will be handed over and taken alive;

sentences.zh: 百姓畏蕃戎之來，有財必盡為所掠。

translations.literal: the common people fear the coming of the barbarians; any wealth they have will surely be entirely plundered by them.
translations.idiomatic: the people dread the arrival of the Tibetans, knowing that whatever wealth they have will be stripped away.

sentences.zh: 是以順於王化者其心不得不怠，陷於寇境者其勢不得不堅。」

translations.literal: Therefore those who submit to royal transformation must slacken in heart, and those trapped in rebel territory must stiffen in resolve."
translations.idiomatic: Thus those loyal to the throne must lose heart, while those under rebel rule must harden their resistance."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「今懷光別保蒲、絳，吐蕃遠避封疆，形勢既分，腹背無患，瑊、晟諸帥，才力得伸。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Now Huai Guang holds Pu and Jiang separately, and the Tibetans have withdrawn far from the border; with the situation thus divided and no threat front or rear, Jian, Sheng, and the other commanders can fully exert their talents."
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "Li Huai Guang now holds Pu and Jiang on his own, and the Tibetans have retreated far from our borders. With threats divided and no enemy at front or back, Jian, Sheng, and the other generals can at last fight to their full strength."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「但願陛下慎於撫接，勤於砥礪，中興大業，旬月可期，不宜尚眷眷於犬羊之群，以失將士之情也。」

translations.literal: He also said: "I only wish Your Majesty would be careful in reassuring and supporting them and diligent in sharpening their resolve; the great work of restoration can be expected within ten days or a month. It is not fitting still to dote on that pack of dogs and sheep and thereby lose the affection of officers and soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "If Your Majesty handles them with care and keeps their edge honed, restoration may be achieved within weeks. You should not keep pinning your hopes on that pack of wolves and sheep at the cost of your own army's loyalty."

sentences.zh: 上復使謂贄曰：「卿言吐蕃形勢甚善，然瑊、晟諸軍當議規畫，今其進取。

translations.literal: The emperor again had someone tell Zhi: "Your analysis of the Tibetan situation is very good; yet Jian, Sheng, and the other armies should be consulted on plans for their advance now.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent word to Zhi again: "Your assessment of the Tibetans is excellent, but Jian, Sheng, and the other armies should now be consulted on how to advance.

sentences.zh: 朕欲遣使宣慰，卿宜審細條疏以聞。」

translations.literal: I wish to send an envoy to announce comfort; you should carefully itemize and report in detail."
translations.idiomatic: I intend to dispatch an envoy to rally them. Prepare a detailed memorandum for my review."

sentences.zh: 贄以為：「賢君選將，委任責成，故能有功。

translations.literal: Zhi believed: "A worthy ruler selects generals, entrusts them with responsibility, and holds them to results—thus achievement is possible.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi replied: "Wise rulers choose their generals, give them full authority, and hold them accountable—that is how victories are won.

sentences.zh: 況今秦、梁千里，兵勢無常，遙為規畫，未必合宜。

translations.literal: Moreover, Qin and Liang are now a thousand li apart and military conditions are ever shifting; to plan from afar may not fit the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Liang are a thousand li apart and the battlefield shifts by the hour—plans drawn from a distance may not suit conditions at all.

sentences.zh: 彼違命則失君威，從命則害軍事，進退羈礙，難以成功。

translations.literal: If they disobey orders, imperial authority is lost; if they obey, military affairs may suffer harm—advance and retreat both fettered, success is hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Disobey and they undermine your authority; obey and they may botch the campaign—fettered either way, they cannot win.

sentences.zh: 不若假以便宜之權，待以殊常之賞，則將帥感悅，智勇得伸。」

translations.literal: Better to grant them discretionary power and reward them with extraordinary bounty; then the commanders will be moved with gratitude and wisdom and courage can be fully deployed."
translations.idiomatic: Better to grant them discretionary authority and promise exceptional rewards—then the generals will give their all and wit and valor alike can be brought to bear."

sentences.zh: 乃上奏，其略曰：「鋒鏑交於原野而決策於九重之中，機會變於斯須而定計於千里之外，用捨相礙，否臧皆凶。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial, in summary saying: "Spears and blades clash on the open field while decisions are made within the ninefold palace; opportunities shift in an instant while plans are fixed a thousand li away—use and rejection obstruct each other, and whether right or wrong, all brings calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again, in substance: "Blades meet on the plain while strategy is debated in the inner palace; moments of opportunity pass while orders travel a thousand li—every choice entangled, every outcome a disaster.

sentences.zh: 上有掣肘之譏，下無死餒之志。」

translations.literal: Above, there is the reproach of pulling back the elbow; below, there is no will to die of hunger."
translations.idiomatic: The throne invites the charge of micromanagement; the ranks lose the will to fight to the death."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「傳聞與指實不同，懸算與臨事有異。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Rumor differs from what is actually pointed at; calculations in the abstract differ from facing events on the ground."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Reports differ from reality, and plans hatched at a distance differ from the demands of the field."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「設使其中或有肆情干命者，陛下能於此時戮其違詔之罪乎？

translations.literal: He also said: "Suppose among them there are some who act on impulse against orders—could Your Majesty at such a time execute them for the crime of defying an edict?
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "Suppose some of them take unauthorized action—could Your Majesty, at that distance, actually punish them for disobeying an edict?

sentences.zh: 是則違命者既不果行罰，從命者又未必合宜，徒費空言，只勞睿慮，匪惟無益，其損實多。」

translations.literal: If so, those who disobey cannot in fact be punished, while those who obey may not necessarily fit the situation—empty words wasted, sagely thought wearied alone; not only is there no benefit, the harm is in truth great."
translations.idiomatic: Disobedience could not be punished in time; obedience might still be wrong. You would waste words and burden yourself with worry—not merely useless, but actively harmful."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「君上之權，特異臣下，惟不自用，乃能用人。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The sovereign's authority is wholly unlike that of his subjects; only by not wielding it oneself can one employ others."
translations.idiomatic: He concluded: "A ruler's power differs from a subject's—the sovereign who does not do everything himself is the one who can truly use men."

sentences.zh: 癸酉，涇王侹薨。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Prince Tuo of Jing died.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day, Prince Tuo of Jing passed away.

sentences.zh: 徐、海、沂、密觀察使高承宗卒，甲戌，使其子明應知軍事。

translations.literal: Gao Chengzong, regional inspector of Xu, Hai, Yi, and Mi, died; on jiaxu his son Mingying was made acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chengzong, the regional inspector of Xu, Hai, Yi, and Mi, died. On the jiaxu day his son Mingying was placed in charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，李抱真、王武俊距貝州三十里而軍。

translations.literal: On yihai, Li Baozhen and Wang Wujun encamped thirty li from Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day, Li Baozhen and Wang Wujun encamped thirty li from Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 朱滔聞兩軍將至，急召馬寔，寔晝夜兼行赴之。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao, hearing the two armies were approaching, urgently summoned Ma Shi; Shi traveled day and night to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao learned both armies were nearing, he urgently recalled Ma Shi, who forced the march day and night to reach him.

sentences.zh: 或謂滔曰：「武俊善野戰，不可當其鋒，宜徙營稍前逼之，使回紇絕其糧道。

translations.literal: Someone said to Tao: "Wujun excels at field fighting; one cannot meet his sharp edge head-on. It would be better to shift camp slightly forward to press him, and have the Uyghurs cut off his grain route.
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised Tao: "Wujun is master of open battle—you cannot meet his charge. Shift camp forward to press him and have the Uyghurs sever his supply lines.

sentences.zh: 我坐食德、棣之餫，依營而陳，利則進攻，否則入保，待其饑疲，然後可制也。」

translations.literal: We would sit and eat the grain of De and Di, array our forces by camp, advance if advantageous and otherwise fall back to defense, wait until they are hungry and weary, and then they can be controlled."
translations.idiomatic: We would live off the grain of De and Di, fight from fortified camps, strike when the odds favor us and withdraw when they do not, and break them only after hunger and exhaustion have done their work."

sentences.zh: 滔疑未決。

translations.literal: Tao hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Tao wavered, unable to decide.

sentences.zh: 會馬寔軍至，滔命明日出戰。

translations.literal: Just then Ma Shi's army arrived; Tao ordered battle the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shi's army arrived just then, and Tao ordered an attack for the following day.

sentences.zh: 寔言：「軍士冒暑困憊，請休息數日乃戰。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "The soldiers, sore from heat and weary, ask to rest several days before fighting."
translations.idiomatic: Shi pleaded: "The men are worn down by the heat—let them rest a few days before we fight."

sentences.zh: 常侍楊布、將軍蔡雄引回紇達干見滔，達干曰：「回紇在國與鄰國戰，常以五百騎破鄰國數千騎，如掃葉耳。

translations.literal: Regular attendant Yang Bu and general Cai Xiong brought the Uyghur commander Daghan to see Tao. Daghan said: "In our country when we fight neighboring states, five hundred horsemen often rout several thousand enemy horsemen—it is like sweeping leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bu, a regular attendant, and General Cai Xiong presented the Uyghur commander Daghan to Tao. Daghan said: "Back home we routinely rout thousands of enemy cavalry with five hundred riders—it is like sweeping fallen leaves.

sentences.zh: 今受大王金帛、牛酒前後無算，思為大王立效，此其時矣。

translations.literal: Now having received the Great King's gold, silk, cattle, and wine beyond counting, we wish to render service to the Great King—this is the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has lavished gold, silk, cattle, and wine on us beyond measure. We are eager to repay you—now is the time.

sentences.zh: 明日，願大王駐馬高丘，觀回紇為大王翦武俊之騎，使匹馬不返。」

translations.literal: Tomorrow, may the Great King halt his horse on a high knoll and watch the Uyghurs for the Great King cut down Wujun's cavalry so that not a single horse returns."
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow, take your stand on a height and watch us cut Wujun's cavalry to pieces—not one horse will ride back."

sentences.zh: 布、雄曰：「大王英略蓋世，舉燕、薊全軍，將掃河南，清關中，今見小敵□豫不擊，失遠近之望，將何以成霸業乎！

translations.literal: Bu and Xiong said: "Great King, your heroic strategy surpasses the age; raising the full armies of Yan and Ji, you were about to sweep Henan and clear Guanzhong—yet now, facing a small enemy, you are hesitant and will not strike, losing the hope of near and far—how then will you accomplish a hegemon's enterprise!
translations.idiomatic: Bu and Xiong said: "Your strategy is unmatched; you marched the armies of Yan and Ji to sweep Henan and secure Guanzhong—yet now you hesitate before a minor foe and refuse to fight, forfeiting the loyalty of allies near and far. How can you build an empire on that?

sentences.zh: 達干請戰是也。」

translations.literal: Daghan's request for battle is right."
translations.idiomatic: Daghan is right to ask for battle."

sentences.zh: 滔喜，遂決意出戰。

translations.literal: Tao was pleased and thereupon made up his mind to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Pleased, Tao resolved to fight.

sentences.zh: 丙子旦，武俊遣其兵馬使趙琳將五百騎伏於桑林，抱真列方陳於後，武俊引騎兵居前，自當回紇。

translations.literal: At dawn on bingzi, Wujun sent his army-and-horse commissioner Zhao Lin with five hundred horsemen to lie in ambush in mulberry groves; Baozhen drew up a square formation behind, and Wujun led cavalry to the fore, personally blocking the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the bingzi day, Wujun hid five hundred riders under Zhao Lin in a mulberry grove. Baozhen formed a square phalanx to the rear while Wujun took the cavalry vanguard and personally faced the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 回紇縱兵沖之，武俊命其騎控馬避之。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs unleashed their troops in a charge; Wujun ordered his horsemen to rein in and give way.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs charged; Wujun ordered his riders to rein in and yield ground.

sentences.zh: 回紇突出其後，將還，武俊乃縱兵擊之，趙琳自林中出橫擊之，回紇敗走。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs broke through to his rear and were about to withdraw; Wujun then unleashed his troops to strike them, and Zhao Lin sallied from the grove to hit them crosswise—the Uyghurs were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs punched through to his rear and wheeled to withdraw; Wujun then counterattacked, and Zhao Lin burst from the grove to strike their flank. The Uyghurs broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 武俊急追之，滔騎兵亦走，自踐其步陳，步騎皆東奔，滔不能制，遂走趣其營，抱真、武俊合兵追擊之。

translations.literal: Wujun pressed the pursuit hotly; Tao's cavalry also fled, trampling their own infantry formation; infantry and cavalry all fled east; Tao could not control them and ran toward his camp; Baozhen and Wujun combined forces to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun pressed hard after them. Tao's cavalry routed as well, stampeding through their own infantry. Foot and horse alike fled eastward beyond Tao's control; he bolted for his camp while Baozhen and Wujun merged their forces in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 時滔引三萬人出戰，死者萬餘人，逃潰者亦萬餘人，滔才與數千人入營堅守。

translations.literal: At that time Tao had led thirty thousand men into battle; more than ten thousand were dead and more than ten thousand scattered in flight; Tao had only a few thousand left to enter camp and hold fast.
translations.idiomatic: Tao had marched out with thirty thousand men. More than ten thousand were killed and another ten thousand fled in disorder. Only a few thousand remained with Tao to hold the camp.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，昏霧，兩軍不能進，抱真軍其營之西北，武俊軍其東北。

translations.literal: It happened to be dusk and misty gloom; neither army could advance; Baozhen encamped northwest of Tao's camp and Wujun northeast of it.
translations.idiomatic: Dusk fell and thick mist rolled in, halting both pursuers. Baozhen camped northwest of Tao's position and Wujun to the northeast.

sentences.zh: 滔夜焚營，引兵出南門，趣德州遁去，委棄所掠資貨山積。

translations.literal: At night Tao burned his camp, led his troops out the south gate, fled toward Dezhou, and abandoned plunder and goods heaped like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: That night Tao burned his camp, marched out the south gate, and fled toward Dezhou, leaving mountains of loot behind.

sentences.zh: 兩軍以霧，不能追也。

translations.literal: Because of the mist, the two armies could not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: The mist kept both armies from giving chase.

sentences.zh: 滔殺楊布、蔡雄而歸幽州，心既內慚，又恐范陽留守劉怦因敗圖己。

translations.literal: Tao killed Yang Bu and Cai Xiong and returned to Youzhou; inwardly ashamed, he also feared that Liu Ping, garrison commander of Fanyang, would use his defeat to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao executed Yang Bu and Cai Xiong and withdrew to Youzhou, ashamed at heart and fearful that Liu Ping, the Fanyang garrison commander, would exploit his defeat to move against him.

sentences.zh: 怦悉發留守兵夾道二十里，具儀仗，迎之入府，相對悲喜，時人多之。

translations.literal: Ping mustered all garrison troops for twenty li along the road, prepared ceremonial escort, welcomed him into the headquarters, and face to face they wept and rejoiced—the people of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ping deployed the entire garrison along twenty li of road with full ceremonial escort, welcomed Tao into headquarters, and together they wept and laughed by turns. People far and wide praised his grace.

sentences.zh: 初，張孝忠以易州歸國，詔以孝忠為義武節度使，以易、定、滄三州隸之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Xiaozhong submitted Yizhou to the dynasty; an edict made Xiaozhong military governor of Yiwu and placed Yi, Ding, and Cang under him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhang Xiaozhong surrendered Yizhou to the court, he was appointed military governor of Yiwu with Yi, Ding, and Cang placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 滄州刺史李固烈，李惟岳之妻兄也，請歸恆州，孝忠遣押牙安喜程華交其州事。

translations.literal: Cangzhou prefect Li Gulei, elder brother-in-law of Li Weiyue, asked to return to Hengzhou; Xiaozhong sent his aide Cheng Hua of Anxi to hand over provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gulei, prefect of Cangzhou and brother-in-law of Li Weiyue, asked to return to Hengzhou. Xiaozhong sent his staff officer Cheng Hua of Anxi to transfer authority over the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 固烈悉取軍府綾、縑、珍貨數十車，將行，軍士大噪曰：「刺史掃府庫之實以行，將士於後饑寒，奈何！」

translations.literal: Gulei took all the damask, silk, and precious goods of the military headquarters—dozens of cartloads—and was about to depart when the soldiers raised a great clamor: "The prefect is emptying the treasury and leaving—what of us soldiers left behind, hungry and cold!"
translations.idiomatic: Gulei loaded dozens of carts with damask, silk bolts, and precious goods from the headquarters and prepared to leave. The troops erupted in uproar: "The prefect is stripping the treasury bare and walking away—what about us, left hungry and cold?"

sentences.zh: 遂殺固烈，屠其家。

translations.literal: They thereupon killed Gulei and slaughtered his household.
translations.idiomatic: They killed Gulei on the spot and massacred his family.

sentences.zh: 程華聞亂，自竇逃出，亂兵求得之，請知州事。

translations.literal: Cheng Hua, hearing the disorder, escaped through a hole in the wall; the mutineers found him and asked him to take charge of provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the riot, Cheng Hua slipped out through a breach in the wall. The mutineers tracked him down and asked him to govern the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 華不得已，從之。

translations.literal: Hua had no choice but to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Hua had no choice but to agree.

sentences.zh: 孝忠聞之，即版華攝滄州刺史。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhong heard of this, he immediately issued a commission making Hua acting prefect of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhong learned of this, he promptly appointed Hua acting prefect of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 華素寬厚，推心以待將士，將士安之。

translations.literal: Hua was by nature generous and magnanimous; he treated the officers and soldiers with open heart, and they were reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was naturally magnanimous and won the troops over with genuine trust. They settled down under his rule.

sentences.zh: 會朱滔、王武俊叛，更遣人招華，華皆不從。

translations.literal: When Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun rebelled, they again sent men to win Hua over, but Hua would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun rose in rebellion, each sent envoys to win Hua over; he refused them both.

sentences.zh: 時孝忠在定州，自滄如定，必過瀛州，瀛隸朱滔，道路阻澀。

translations.literal: At the time Xiaozhong was at Dingzhou; going from Cang to Ding one had to pass Yingzhou, which was under Zhu Tao, and the road was blocked and difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong was then at Dingzhou. The route from Cangzhou to Dingzhou passed through Yingzhou, which belonged to Zhu Tao, making communication perilous.

sentences.zh: 滄州錄事參軍李宇說華，表陳利害，請別為一軍，華從之，遣宇奉表詣行在。

translations.literal: Cangzhou recorder Li Yu persuaded Hua to memorialize setting forth advantage and harm and request separate status as an army; Hua agreed and sent Yu to present the memorial at the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, a recorder at Cangzhou, urged Hua to petition the throne with the strategic stakes and request independent army status. Hua agreed and sent Yu to the imperial camp with the memorial.

sentences.zh: 上即以華為滄州刺史、橫海軍副大使、知節度事，賜名日華，令日華歲供義武租錢十二萬緡。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately made Hua prefect of Cangzhou, vice envoy of the Henghai Army, and director of military governorship affairs; granted him the name Rihua; and ordered Rihua to supply twelve thousand strings of rent money annually to Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately appointed Hua prefect of Cangzhou, deputy commissioner of the Henghai Army, and acting military governor, bestowing the name Rihua and ordering him to pay Yiwu twelve thousand strings of rent annually.

sentences.zh: 王武俊又使人說誘之，時軍中乏馬，日華紿使者曰：「王大夫必欲相屬，當以二百騎相助。」

translations.literal: Wang Wujun again sent men to persuade and entice him; at the time the army lacked horses; Rihua deceived the envoy, saying: "If Great Physician Wang truly wishes me to submit, he must supply two hundred horsemen to assist."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun sent envoys again to win him over. The army was short of horses, and Rihua bluffed the envoy: "If Minister Wang truly wants my allegiance, let him send two hundred cavalry to assist me."

sentences.zh: 武俊給之，日華悉留其馬，遣其士歸。

translations.literal: Wujun supplied them; Rihua kept all their horses and sent their men back.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun complied. Rihua kept every horse and sent the men home.

sentences.zh: 武俊怒，而方與馬燧等相拒，不能攻取，日華由是獲全。

translations.literal: Wujun was angry, but was then resisting Ma Sui and others and could not attack and seize Cangzhou; Rihua thereby preserved himself intact.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun was furious, but he was tied up facing Ma Sui and could not mount an attack—so Rihua remained secure.

sentences.zh: 及武俊歸國，日華乃遣人謝過，償其馬價，且賂之。

translations.literal: When Wujun returned to allegiance to the dynasty, Rihua then sent men to apologize, repay the price of the horses, and also bribe him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wujun submitted to the court again, Rihua sent envoys to apologize, repay the horses' value, and offer gifts besides.

sentences.zh: 武俊喜，復與交好。

translations.literal: Wujun was pleased and renewed friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun was mollified and resumed friendly ties.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，李晟大陳兵，諭以收復京城。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Li Sheng drew up his troops in great array and addressed them on recovering the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day, Li Sheng paraded his army in full formation and roused the men to retake the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是，姚令言等屢遣諜人覘晟進軍之期，皆為邏騎所獲。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yao Lingyan and the others had repeatedly sent spies to scout the date of Sheng's advance; all were captured by patrol horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Lingyan and the other rebel leaders had repeatedly sent spies to learn when Sheng would march; patrol riders captured every one.

sentences.zh: 晟引示以所陳兵，謂曰：「歸語諸賊，努力固守，勿不忠於賊也！」

translations.literal: Sheng brought them to view the arrayed troops and said: "Go back and tell the rebels: strive to hold fast—do not be disloyal to the rebels!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng paraded the prisoners before his assembled troops and told them: "Go back and tell the rebels to hold firm—stay loyal to your masters!"

sentences.zh: 皆飲之酒，給錢而縱之。

translations.literal: He gave them all wine to drink, paid them money, and released them.
translations.idiomatic: He treated them to wine, paid them cash, and let them go.

sentences.zh: 遂引兵至通化門外，曜武而還，賊不敢出。

translations.literal: He then led his troops to outside Tonghua Gate, displayed martial prowess, and returned; the rebels did not dare sally forth.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched to Tonghua Gate, displayed his strength, and withdrew. The rebels did not dare emerge.

sentences.zh: 晟召諸將，問兵所從入，皆請「先取外城，據坊市，然後北攻宮闕。」

translations.literal: Sheng summoned the generals and asked by what route the army should enter; all requested "first take the outer city, hold the wards and markets, and then attack the palace compound from the north."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng gathered his generals and asked which route the army should take. All urged: "Take the outer city first, secure the wards and markets, then strike the palace from the north."

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「坊市狹隘，賊若伏兵格鬥，居人驚亂，非官軍之利也。

translations.literal: Sheng said: "The wards and markets are narrow and cramped; if the rebels lay ambush and fight hand to hand, the residents will panic and scatter—this is not to the official army's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng replied: "The wards are cramped alleys. If the rebels ambush us there, civilians will panic in the fighting—conditions that favor them, not us.

sentences.zh: 今賊重兵皆聚苑中，不若自苑北攻之，潰其腹心，賊必奔亡。

translations.literal: Now the rebels' main force is all gathered in the imperial park; better to attack from the north of the park, break their heart, and the rebels will surely flee.
translations.idiomatic: Their main force is massed in the imperial park. Better to attack from the north, strike at their heart, and they will collapse and run.

sentences.zh: 如此，則宮闕不殘，坊市無擾，策之上者也！」

translations.literal: In this way the palace will not be damaged, the wards and markets will not be disturbed—it is the superior strategy!"
translations.idiomatic: The palace would be spared, the city undisturbed—that is the best plan!"

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「善！」

translations.literal: All the generals said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: The generals all assented: "Excellent!"

sentences.zh: 乃牒渾瑊及鎮國節度使駱元光、商州節度使尚可孤，刻期集於城下，壬辰，尚可孤敗泚將仇敬忠於藍田西，斬之。

translations.literal: He then dispatched orders to Hun Jian, Lu Yuan Guang of the Zhenguo military governorship, and Shang Ke'gu of the Shangzhou military governorship, fixing a date to assemble below the city wall; on renchen, Shang Ke'gu defeated Zhu Ci's general Qiu Jingzhong west of Lantian and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He issued orders to Hun Jian, Lu Yuan Guang the Zhenguo military governor, and Shang Ke'gu the Shangzhou military governor to rendezvous at the walls on a fixed date. On the renchen day, Shang Ke'gu routed Zhu Ci's general Qiu Jingzhong west of Lantian and took his head.

sentences.zh: 乙未，李晟移軍於光泰門外米倉村。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Li Sheng moved his army to Micang Village outside Guangtai Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day, Li Sheng relocated his army to Micang Village outside Guangtai Gate.

sentences.zh: 丙申，晟方自臨築壘，泚驍將張庭芝、李希傅引兵大至，晟謂諸將曰：「始吾憂賊潛匿不出，今來送死，此天讚我，不可失也！」

translations.literal: On bingshen day, Sheng was personally overseeing the building of ramparts when Zhu Ci's fierce generals Zhang Tingzhi and Li Xifu led their troops up in force. Sheng said to his generals: "At first I worried the rebels would lie hidden and not come out; now they come to deliver themselves to death. Heaven is aiding us—we must not miss this chance!"
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day, Li Sheng was personally supervising the construction of fortifications when Zhu Ci's crack generals Zhang Tingzhi and Li Xifu marched up in strength. Sheng told his officers: "I had feared the rebels would stay hidden and refuse to fight; now they come to throw away their lives. Heaven favors us—this chance must not be lost!"

sentences.zh: 命副元帥兵馬使吳詵等縱兵擊之。

translations.literal: He ordered the deputy commander of army and horses Wu Shen and others to unleash their troops and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his deputy commander of army and horses, Wu Shen, and the others to unleash their troops and attack.

sentences.zh: 時華州營在北，兵少，賊並力攻之，晟命牙前將李演等帥精兵救之。

translations.literal: At the time the Huazhou camp was to the north and had few troops; the rebels combined their strength to attack it. Sheng ordered the vanguard general Li Yan and others to lead elite troops to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: The Huazhou camp lay to the north with too few men, and the rebels massed to crush it. Sheng sent the vanguard general Li Yan and others with picked troops to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 演等力戰，賊敗走。

translations.literal: Yan and the others fought hard; the rebels were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and his men fought fiercely and put the rebels to flight.

sentences.zh: 演等追之，乘勝入光泰門，再戰，又破之。

translations.literal: Yan and the others pursued them, and riding their victory entered Guangtai Gate; they fought again and broke the enemy once more.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued the fleeing rebels, burst through Guangtai Gate in the heat of victory, fought again, and broke them a second time.

sentences.zh: 會夜，晟斂兵還。

translations.literal: As night fell, Sheng gathered his troops and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Night came on, and Sheng recalled his troops.

sentences.zh: 賊餘眾走入白華門，夜，聞慟哭。

translations.literal: The rebels' remaining troops fled into Baihua Gate; at night, wailing was heard.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel survivors fled into Baihua Gate; that night, sounds of bitter weeping could be heard.

sentences.zh: 希傅，希烈之弟也。

translations.literal: Xifu was the younger brother of Xilie.
translations.idiomatic: Xifu was Li Xilie's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，晟復出兵，諸將請待西師至，夾攻之。

translations.literal: On dingyou day, Sheng again deployed his army. The generals asked to wait until the western army arrived to attack from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day Sheng marched out again. His generals urged him to wait for the western army and strike the rebels from both sides.

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「賊數敗，已破膽，不乘勝取之，使其成備，非計也。」

translations.literal: Sheng said: "The rebels have been defeated time and again and have already lost their nerve. If we do not take them while we have the advantage and let them finish their preparations, that is no strategy at all."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "The rebels have been beaten repeatedly and have lost their nerve. If we fail to press our advantage and let them recover and fortify, that is no strategy at all."

sentences.zh: 賊又出戰，官軍屢捷。

translations.literal: The rebels came out to fight again; the imperial army won victory after victory.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sallied forth again, and the imperial army won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 駱元光敗泚眾於滻西。

translations.literal: Luo Yuanguang defeated Zhu Ci's forces west of the Chan River.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yuanguang routed Zhu Ci's army west of the Chan River.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，晟陳兵於光泰門外，使李演及牙前兵馬使王佖將騎兵，牙前將史萬頃將步兵，直抵苑牆神{鹿加}村。

translations.literal: On wuxu day, Sheng drew up his troops outside Guangtai Gate. He sent Li Yan and the vanguard army-and-horses commissioner Wang Bi to lead the cavalry, and the vanguard general Shi Wanqing to lead the infantry, straight to Shenlu Village at the park wall.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day Sheng arrayed his forces outside Guangtai Gate, sending Li Yan and the vanguard cavalry commissioner Wang Bi with the horsemen and the vanguard general Shi Wanqing with the foot soldiers straight to Shenlu Village at the imperial park wall.

sentences.zh: 晟先使人夜開苑牆二百餘步，比演等至，賊已樹柵塞之，自柵中刺射官軍，官軍不得進。

translations.literal: Sheng had men open two hundred-plus paces in the park wall by night. By the time Yan and the others arrived, the rebels had already erected palisades to block the gap, and from within the palisades they thrust and shot at the imperial army, which could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had sent men by night to breach more than two hundred paces of the park wall, but by the time Yan's force arrived the rebels had already thrown up palisades to seal the gap and were stabbing and shooting from behind them. The imperial army could not get through.

sentences.zh: 晟怒，叱諸將曰：「縱賊如此，吾先斬公輩矣！」

translations.literal: Sheng was furious and berated his generals: "You let the rebels act like this—in your place I would first cut off your heads!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng flew into a rage and shouted at his generals: "If you let the rebels get away with this, I'll cut off your heads first!"

sentences.zh: 萬頃懼，帥眾先進，拔柵而入，佖、演引騎兵繼之，賊眾大潰，諸軍分道並入。

translations.literal: Wanqing was terrified and led his men forward first, tore out the palisades and entered; Bi and Yan led the cavalry after them. The rebel host broke in great rout, and the armies entered by separate routes together.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Wanqing led his men forward, tore down the palisades, and broke through; Bi and Yan followed with the cavalry. The rebel host collapsed in rout, and the imperial armies poured in by every route at once.

sentences.zh: 姚令言等猶力戰，晟命決勝軍使唐良臣等步騎蹙之，且戰且前，凡十餘合，賊不能支。

translations.literal: Yao Lingyan and the others still fought hard. Sheng ordered the Victory Army commissioner Tang Liangchen and others with infantry and cavalry to press them; fighting as they advanced, for more than ten clashes the rebels could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Lingyan and his men still fought stubbornly. Sheng ordered Tang Liangchen and others of the Victory Army to press them with foot and horse, advancing battle by battle through more than ten engagements until the rebels could hold no longer.

sentences.zh: 至白華門，有賊數千騎出官軍之背，晟帥百餘騎回御之，左右呼曰：「相公來！」

translations.literal: At Baihua Gate, several thousand rebel horsemen emerged behind the imperial army. Sheng led a hundred-plus horsemen to turn and meet them; men on either side cried: "The Chancellor comes!"
translations.idiomatic: At Baihua Gate several thousand rebel horsemen struck from behind the imperial line. Sheng wheeled about with a little over a hundred riders to meet them, while men on either flank shouted: "The Chancellor comes!"

sentences.zh: 賊皆驚潰。

translations.literal: The rebels all fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke and fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 先是，泚遣張光晟將兵五千屯九曲，去東渭橋十餘里，光晟密輸款於晟。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhu Ci had sent Zhang Guangsheng with five thousand troops to camp at Jiuqu, more than ten li from East Weiqiao Bridge; Guangsheng secretly offered his allegiance to Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhu Ci had posted Zhang Guangsheng with five thousand men at Jiuqu, a little over ten li from East Weiqiao Bridge. Guangsheng had secretly pledged himself to Sheng.

sentences.zh: 及泚敗，光晟勸泚出亡。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci was defeated, Guangsheng urged Zhu Ci to flee.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci's cause collapsed, Guangsheng urged him to flee.

sentences.zh: 泚乃與姚令言帥餘眾西走，猶近萬人。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci then fled west with Yao Lingyan at the head of the remaining troops—still nearly ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci then fled west with Yao Lingyan and the survivors—still nearly ten thousand strong.

sentences.zh: 光晟送泚出城，還，降於晟。

translations.literal: Guangsheng escorted Zhu Ci out of the city, then returned and surrendered to Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsheng saw Zhu Ci out of the city, then returned and surrendered to Sheng.

sentences.zh: 晟遣兵馬使田子奇以騎兵追泚。

translations.literal: Sheng dispatched the army-and-horses commissioner Tian Ziqi with cavalry to pursue Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng sent the cavalry commissioner Tian Ziqi in pursuit of Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 晟頓含元殿前，捨於右金吾仗，令諸軍曰：「晟賴將士之力，克清宮禁。

translations.literal: Sheng halted before Hanyuan Hall and lodged at the Right Jinwu Guard post. He ordered the armies: "Sheng has relied on the valor of officers and soldiers to cleanse the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng halted before Hanyuan Hall and took quarters at the Right Jinwu Guard station. He addressed the armies: "By the strength of officers and soldiers, we have cleared the palace precincts.

sentences.zh: 長安士庶，久陷賊庭，若小有震驚，非弔民伐罪之意。

translations.literal: The people of Chang'an have long been trapped in the rebel domain; if we cause the slightest alarm, that is not the spirit of comforting the people and punishing crime.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chang'an have long suffered under rebel rule. The least disturbance would betray the purpose of comforting the people and punishing the guilty.

sentences.zh: 晟與公等室家相見非晚，五日內無得通家信。」

translations.literal: It will not be long before Sheng and you meet your wives and children; within five days you may not send letters home."
translations.idiomatic: It will not be long before I and you are reunited with our families. For five days, no one may send word home."

sentences.zh: 命京兆尹李齊運等安慰居人。

translations.literal: He ordered the Jingzhao Prefect Li Qiyun and others to reassure the residents.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Jingzhao prefect Li Qiyun and others to reassure the city's inhabitants.

sentences.zh: 晟大將高明曜取賊妓，尚可孤軍士擅取賊馬，晟皆斬之，軍中股慄。

translations.literal: Sheng's great general Gao Mingyao took a rebel courtesan; Shang Kegu's soldiers seized rebel horses on their own authority; Sheng executed them all, and throughout the army legs trembled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's senior general Gao Mingyao took a rebel courtesan for himself, and soldiers under Shang Kegu helped themselves to rebel horses. Sheng had them all executed, and the whole army trembled.

sentences.zh: 公私安堵，秋毫無犯，遠坊有經宿乃知官軍入城者。

translations.literal: Public and private quarters were tranquil; not the slightest thing was violated—so quiet that in distant wards some only learned the imperial army had entered the city after a night had passed.
translations.idiomatic: Public and private life remained undisturbed; not the smallest thing was touched. In outlying wards some inhabitants only learned the imperial army had entered after a full night had passed.

sentences.zh: 是日，渾瑊、戴休顏、韓游瑰亦克咸陽，敗賊三千餘眾，聞泚西走，分兵邀之。

translations.literal: That same day, Hun Jian, Dai Xiuyan, and Han Yougui also took Xianyang and defeated more than three thousand rebels. Hearing Zhu Ci had fled west, they split their forces to intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Hun Jian, Dai Xiuyan, and Han Yougui also recovered Xianyang and routed more than three thousand rebels. Learning that Zhu Ci had fled west, they divided their forces to cut him off.

sentences.zh: 己亥，晟使京西兵馬使孟涉頓白華門，尚可孤屯望仙門，駱元光屯章敬寺，晟以牙前三千人屯安國寺，以鎮京城。

translations.literal: On jihai day, Sheng had the Jingxi army-and-horses commissioner Meng She encamp at Baihua Gate, Shang Kegu camp at Wangxian Gate, Luo Yuanguang camp at Zhangjing Temple; Sheng himself stationed three thousand vanguard troops at Anguo Temple to garrison the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day Sheng posted the Jingxi cavalry commissioner Meng She at Baihua Gate, Shang Kegu at Wangxian Gate, and Luo Yuanguang at Zhangjing Temple, while he himself kept three thousand vanguard troops at Anguo Temple to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 斬泚黨李希倩、敬釭、彭偃等八人於市。

translations.literal: Eight of Zhu Ci's partisans—Li Xiqian, Jing Gang, Peng Yan, and others—were executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Eight of Zhu Ci's followers—Li Xiqian, Jing Gang, Peng Yan, and others—were executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 王武俊既破朱滔，還恆州，表讓幽州、盧龍節度使，上許之。

translations.literal: Wang Wujun, having defeated Zhu Tao, returned to Hengzhou and memorialized to yield the posts of military governor of Youzhou and Lulong; the emperor granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Zhu Tao, Wang Wujun returned to Hengzhou and asked to relinquish the posts of military governor of Youzhou and Lulong. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸卯，李晟遣掌書記吳人于公異作露布上行在曰：「臣已肅清宮禁，祗謁寢園，鐘虡不移，廟貌如故。」

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guimao day, Li Sheng sent his secretarial aide Yu Gongyi, a man of Wu, to draft a victory bulletin to the imperial camp, stating: "Your subject has purged the palace precincts and reverently visited the imperial tombs; bells and ritual vessels stand unmoved, the temple aspect unchanged as before."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guimao day, Li Sheng had his secretarial aide Yu Gongyi, a native of Wu, compose a victory bulletin to the imperial camp: "Your subject has cleared the palace precincts and reverently visited the imperial tombs. Bells and ritual vessels stand unmoved; the ancestral halls look as they did before."

sentences.zh: 上泣下曰：「天生李晟，以為社稷，非為朕也。」

translations.literal: The emperor wept and said: "Heaven gave us Li Sheng for the altars of state—not for me alone."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and said: "Heaven sent Li Sheng for the altars of state—not for me alone."

sentences.zh: 晟在渭橋，熒惑守歲，久之乃退，賓佐皆賀，曰：「熒惑退捨，皇家之福也！

translations.literal: Sheng was at Weiqiao Bridge when Mars lingered at the Year Star; only after a long while did it withdraw. His staff all congratulated him, saying: "When Mars withdraws from the Year Star, that is fortune for the house of Tang!
translations.idiomatic: At Weiqiao Bridge, Mars had lingered at the Year Star and only after a long while withdrew. Sheng's staff congratulated him, saying: "When Mars withdraws from the Year Star, that is fortune for the dynasty!

sentences.zh: 宜速進兵。」

translations.literal: We should advance at once."
translations.idiomatic: We should march at once."

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「天子野次，臣下知死敵而已。

translations.literal: Sheng said: "The Son of Heaven is encamped in the open; his subjects know only to die fighting the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng replied: "The Son of Heaven is encamped in the wilderness; his servants know only to die fighting the enemy.

sentences.zh: 天象高遠，誰得知之！」

translations.literal: The celestial signs are lofty and remote—who can say what they mean!"
translations.idiomatic: The heavens are far above us—who can read their meaning!"

sentences.zh: 既克長安，乃謂之曰：「曏非相拒也，吾聞五星贏、縮無常，萬一復來守歲，吾軍不戰自潰矣！」

translations.literal: After Chang'an was recovered, he told them: "Before I was not refusing you—I have heard that the Five Planets wax and wane without fixed rule; if by chance Mars should again linger at the Year Star, our army would break without fighting!"
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an fell, he told them: "I was not rejecting your counsel. I know the Five Planets wax and wane without fixed rule; if Mars should again linger at the Year Star, our army would collapse without a battle!"

sentences.zh: 皆謝曰：「非所及也！」

translations.literal: They all apologized: "We did not grasp that!"
translations.idiomatic: They all apologized: "That was beyond us!"

sentences.zh: 朱泚將奔吐蕃，其眾隨道散亡，比至涇州，才百餘騎。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci was about to flee toward the Tibetans; his followers scattered and perished along the road. By the time he reached Jingzhou, he had only a hundred-plus horsemen left.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci meant to flee to the Tibetans, but his followers scattered and died along the road. By the time he reached Jingzhou he had barely a hundred horsemen left.

sentences.zh: 田希鑒閉門拒之，泚謂之曰：「汝之節，吾所授也。

translations.literal: Tian Xijian shut his gates and refused him entry. Zhu Ci said to him: "Your command—I am the one who granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xijian shut his gates and refused him. Zhu Ci said: "Your commission—I am the one who gave it to you.

sentences.zh: 奈何臨危相負！」

translations.literal: How can you turn against me in a crisis!"
translations.idiomatic: How can you abandon me at the hour of danger!"

sentences.zh: 使焚其門。

translations.literal: He had his men burn the gate.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his men to burn the gate.

sentences.zh: 希鑒取節投火中曰：「還汝節！」

translations.literal: Xijian took his commission and threw it into the fire, saying: "Here is your commission back!"
translations.idiomatic: Xijian took his commission of office and cast it into the flames, crying: "Take back your commission!"

sentences.zh: 泚眾皆哭。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci's followers all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci's followers all broke into tears.

sentences.zh: 涇卒遂殺姚令言，詣希鑒降。

translations.literal: The Jingzhou garrison then killed Yao Lingyan and came to Xijian to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingzhou garrison then killed Yao Lingyan and surrendered to Xijian.

sentences.zh: 泚獨與范陽親兵及宗族、賓客北趣驛馬關，寧州刺史夏侯英拒之。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci alone, with his Fanyang personal guard and his clansmen and retainers, headed north toward Yima Pass; the prefect of Ningzhou, Xiahou Ying, barred his way.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci fled north toward Yima Pass with only his Fanyang personal guard, kinsmen, and retainers. Xiahou Ying, prefect of Ningzhou, blocked his path.

sentences.zh: 至彭原西城屯，其將梁庭芬射泚墜坑中，韓旻等斬之，詣涇州降。

translations.literal: Reaching Pengyuan, he encamped at West City. His general Liang Tingfen shot Zhu Ci and knocked him into a pit; Han Min and others beheaded him and went to Jingzhou to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At Pengyuan he encamped at West City. His general Liang Tingfen shot him down into a pit; Han Min and the others beheaded him and took his head to Jingzhou to surrender.

sentences.zh: 源休、李子平奔鳳翔，李楚琳斬之，皆傳首行在。

translations.literal: Yuan Xiu and Li Ziping fled to Fengxiang; Li Chulin executed them, and their heads were sent to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu and Li Ziping fled to Fengxiang, where Li Chulin executed them. Their heads were sent to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 上命陸贄草詔賜渾瑊，使訪求奉天所失裹頭內人。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Lu Zhi to draft an edict for Hun Jian, instructing him to seek out the palace women who had lost their headwraps at Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Lu Zhi to draft an edict for Hun Jian instructing him to search for the palace women who had lost their headwraps at Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 贄上奏，以為：「今巨盜始平，疲瘵之民，瘡痍之卒，尚未循拊，而首訪婦人，非所以副惟新之望也。

translations.literal: Zhi submitted a memorial, arguing: "The great rebel has only just been subdued; the worn and afflicted people and the wounded soldiery have not yet been properly settled and comforted—and yet the first order is to search for women. This does not meet the hopes of renewal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi memorialized the throne: "The great rebel has only just been crushed; the exhausted people and wounded soldiers have not yet been settled and comforted. Yet the first order of business is to hunt for women. That does not fulfill the promise of renewal.

sentences.zh: 謀始盡善，克終已稀；

translations.literal: To plan the beginning with full perfection but to finish is already rare;
translations.idiomatic: To plan the beginning perfectly is hard enough; to carry it through to the end is rarer still;

sentences.zh: 始而不謀，終則何有！

translations.literal: if one does not plan at the start, what can one hope for at the end!
translations.idiomatic: if there is no planning at the start, what can be hoped for at the end!

sentences.zh: 所賜瑊詔，未敢承旨。」

translations.literal: The edict intended for Jian—I dare not carry out its order."
translations.idiomatic: As for the edict intended for Jian, I dare not draft it as ordered."

sentences.zh: 上遂不降詔，竟遣中使求之。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore did not issue the edict but in the end sent a eunuch envoy to search.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore did not issue the edict, but in the end sent a eunuch envoy to conduct the search.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，詔吏部侍郎班宏充宣慰使，勞問將士，撫慰蒸黎。

translations.literal: On yisi day, an edict appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Ban Hong as Commissioner of Comfort to inquire after officers and soldiers and soothe the common people.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day an edict appointed Ban Hong, vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, commissioner of comfort to inquire after the troops and reassure the people.

sentences.zh: 兩午，李晟斬文武官受朱泚寵任者崔宣、洪經綸等十餘人，又表守節不屈者劉乃、蔣沇等。

translations.literal: On bingwu day, Li Sheng executed more than ten civil and military officials who had enjoyed Zhu Ci's favor and trust—Cui Xuan, Hong Jinglun, and others—and also submitted a memorial commending those who had held firm and would not yield—Liu Nai, Jiang Yan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day Li Sheng executed more than ten civil and military officials who had enjoyed Zhu Ci's favor—Cui Xuan, Hong Jinglun, and others—and submitted a memorial commending those who had held firm and refused to submit—Liu Nai, Jiang Yan, and others.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以李晟為司徒、中書令，駱元光、尚可孤各遷官有差，以檢校御史中丞田希鑒為涇原節度使。

translations.literal: On jiyou day, Li Sheng was made Grand Mentor and Grand Chancellor; Luo Yuanguang and Shang Kegu were each promoted by varying degrees; and the Acting Censor-in-Chief Tian Xijian was made military governor of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day Li Sheng was made grand mentor and grand chancellor; Luo Yuanguang and Shang Kegu were promoted by varying degrees; and Tian Xijian, acting censor-in-chief, was appointed military governor of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 詔改梁州為興元府。

translations.literal: An edict changed Liangzhou to Xingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict renamed Liangzhou as Xingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以渾瑊為侍中，韓游瑰、戴休顏各遷官有差。

translations.literal: On jiayin day, Hun Jian was made Palace Secretariat Director; Han Yougui and Dai Xiuyan were each promoted by varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day Hun Jian was made director of the Palace Secretariat; Han Yougui and Dai Xiuyan were promoted by varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 朱泚之敗也，李忠臣奔樊川，擒獲，丙辰，斬之。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci fell, Li Zhongchen fled to Fanchuan and was captured; on bingchen day he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci fell, Li Zhongchen fled to Fanchuan, was captured, and on bingchen day was executed.

sentences.zh: 上問陸贄：「今至鳳翔有迎駕諸軍。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Lu Zhi: "As we now approach Fengxiang, there are many armies coming to welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Lu Zhi: "As we now approach Fengxiang, many armies are coming to welcome the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 形勢甚盛，欲因此遣人代李楚琳，何如？」

translations.literal: Their strength is imposing. I wish to take this occasion to send someone to replace Li Chulin—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Their strength is imposing. I wish to take this opportunity to send someone to replace Li Chulin. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 贄上奏，以為：「如此則事同脅執，以言乎除亂則不武，以言乎務理則不誠，用是時巡，後將安入！

translations.literal: Zhi submitted a memorial, holding that: "If we do this it is the same as coercion; speak of suppressing rebellion and it is not martial; speak of governing well and it is not sincere. If we conduct an imperial progress in this fashion, where shall we enter thereafter!
translations.idiomatic: Zhi memorialized: "To do this would be coercion plain and simple. Speak of suppressing rebellion and it is not martial; speak of governing rightly and it is not sincere. If the imperial progress proceeds in this way, where afterward shall the throne find entry!

sentences.zh: 議者或謂之權，臣竊未諭其理。

translations.literal: Some in the discussion call this expedient policy, but your subject has not yet grasped the principle.
translations.idiomatic: Some call this expedient policy, but your subject cannot see the principle in it.

sentences.zh: 未權之為義，取類權衡，今輦路所經，首行脅奪，易一帥而虧萬乘之義，得一方而結四海之疑，乃是重其所輕而輕其所重，謂之權也，不亦反乎！

translations.literal: The meaning of policy as 'expedient' (quan) is modeled on the balance-scale. Yet now, on the very route of the imperial carriage, the first act is extortion and seizure—replacing one commander at the cost of the honor of the sovereign's ten thousand chariots, gaining one region while arousing suspicion throughout the four seas. That is to weight what should be light and lighten what should be weighty—to call that 'expedient' is it not precisely reversed!
translations.idiomatic: The word for expedient policy, quan, is modeled on the balance-scale. Yet on the very route of the imperial progress the first act is coercion and seizure—replacing one commander at the cost of the sovereign's honor, gaining one region while sowing suspicion across the empire. That is to weight what should be light and lighten what should be heavy. To call that expedient policy—is it not precisely backward!

sentences.zh: 以反道為權，以任數為智，君上行之必失眾，臣下用之必陷身，歷代之所以多喪亂而長奸邪，由此誤也。

translations.literal: To take reversal of the Way as expedient policy and manipulation as wisdom—if the ruler practices this he will surely lose the people; if ministers employ it they will surely ruin themselves. The reason successive ages have seen so much disorder and so much growth of wickedness lies in this very error.
translations.idiomatic: To treat reversal of the Way as expedient policy and scheming as wisdom—if a ruler practices this he will lose the people; if ministers employ it they will destroy themselves. Ages of disorder and the rise of wickedness stem from this very mistake.

sentences.zh: 不如俟奠枕京邑，征授一官，彼喜於恩宥，將奔走不暇，安敢輒有旅拒，復勞誅鋤哉！」

translations.literal: Better to wait until the capital is secure enough to sleep untroubled, then summon him and appoint him to office. Grateful for pardon, he will hurry to obey and have no leisure to refuse; how would he dare raise any armed resistance and invite further punishment!"
translations.idiomatic: Better to wait until the capital is secure enough to sleep in peace, then summon him and appoint him to office. Grateful for mercy, he will hurry to obey and have no time to refuse. How would he dare raise arms and invite further punishment!"

sentences.zh: 戊午，車駕發漢中。

translations.literal: On wuwu day the imperial carriage departed from Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day the imperial carriage set out from Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 李晟綜理長安以備百司，自請至鳳翔迎扈，上不許。

translations.literal: Li Sheng put Chang'an in order to ready it for all the government offices and asked leave to go to Fengxiang to welcome and escort the emperor; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng put Chang'an in order to ready it for the government offices and asked to go to Fengxiang to welcome the emperor. The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 內常侍尹元貞奉使同華，輒詣河中招諭李懷光。

translations.literal: The Inner Palace Attendant Yin Yuanzhen, on mission to Tonghua, went on his own to Hezhong to summon and persuade Li Huaiguang.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant Yin Yuanzhen, on mission to Tonghua, went on his own to Hezhong to summon and reassure Li Huaiguang.

sentences.zh: 晟奏：「元貞矯制擅赦元惡，請理其罪！」

translations.literal: Sheng memorialized: "Yuanzhen forged an edict and on his own authority pardoned the chief villain—I ask that he be punished!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng memorialized: "Yuanzhen forged an edict and on his own authority pardoned the chief villain. I ask that he be punished!"

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙子，車駕至鳳翔，斬喬琳、蔣鎮、張光晟等。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingzi day, the imperial carriage reached Fengxiang. Qiao Lin, Jiang Zhen, Zhang Guangsheng, and others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingzi day the imperial carriage reached Fengxiang. Qiao Lin, Jiang Zhen, Zhang Guangsheng, and others were executed.

sentences.zh: 李晟以光晟雖臣賊，而滅賊亦頗有力，欲全之，上不許。

translations.literal: Li Sheng, because Guangsheng, although he had served the rebels, had also contributed substantially to their defeat, wished to spare him; the emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng, though Guangsheng had served the rebels, had also contributed substantially to their defeat and wished to spare him. The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 副元帥判官高郢數勸李懷光歸款，懷光遣其子璀詣行在謝罪，請束身歸朝。

translations.literal: The deputy commander's aide Gao Ying repeatedly urged Li Huaiguang to submit in good faith. Huaiguang sent his son Cui to the imperial camp to apologize and ask to surrender himself and return to court.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy commander's aide Gao Ying repeatedly urged Li Huaiguang to submit. Huaiguang sent his son Cui to the imperial camp to apologize and ask to surrender himself and return to court.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，詔遣給事中孔巢父繼先除懷光太子太保敕詣河中宣慰，朔方將士悉復官爵如故。

translations.literal: On gengchen day, an edict dispatched the Supervising Secretary Kong Chaofu, following upon the earlier appointment of Huaiguang as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, to Hezhong as Commissioner of Reassurance; all officers and soldiers of Shuofang were restored to their former ranks and titles.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day an edict sent the supervising secretary Kong Chaofu, following the earlier appointment of Huaiguang as grand mentor of the heir apparent, to Hezhong as commissioner of reassurance. All Shuofang officers and soldiers were restored to their former ranks and titles.

sentences.zh: 壬午，車駕至長安，渾瑊、韓游瑰、戴休顏以其眾扈從，李晟、駱元光、尚可孤以其眾奉迎，步騎十餘萬，旌旗數十里，晟謁見上於三橋，先賀平賊，後謝收復之晚，伏路左請罪。

translations.literal: On renwu day the imperial carriage reached Chang'an. Hun Jian, Han Yougui, and Dai Xiuyan escorted with their troops; Li Sheng, Luo Yuanguang, and Shang Kegu welcomed with theirs. Infantry and cavalry numbered more than a hundred thousand; banners and flags stretched for dozens of li. Sheng paid homage to the emperor at Sanqiao Bridge—first congratulating him on the quelling of the rebels, then apologizing for the lateness of the recovery, prostrating himself at the roadside to ask forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day the imperial carriage reached Chang'an. Hun Jian, Han Yougui, and Dai Xiuyan escorted with their troops; Li Sheng, Luo Yuanguang, and Shang Kegu welcomed him with theirs. More than a hundred thousand foot and horse stretched for dozens of li under banners and flags. At Sanqiao Bridge Sheng paid homage to the emperor—first congratulating him on the defeat of the rebels, then apologizing for the lateness of the recovery, prostrating himself at the roadside to ask forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 上駐馬慰撫，為之掩涕，命左右扶上馬。

translations.literal: The emperor reined in his horse to comfort him, wiped away tears for him, and ordered those at his side to help Sheng mount his horse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reined in his horse to comfort him, wiped away tears, and ordered his attendants to help Sheng back into the saddle.

sentences.zh: 至宮，每閒日，輒宴勳臣，賞賜豐渥。

translations.literal: After reaching the palace, on every idle day he would feast the meritorious ministers, with rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: After reaching the palace, on every free day he feasted the meritorious ministers with lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 李晟為之首，渾瑊次之，諸將相又次之。

translations.literal: Li Sheng stood first, Hun Jian second, and the other generals and ministers after them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng came first, Hun Jian second, and the other generals and ministers after them.

sentences.zh: 曹王皋遣其將伊慎、王鍔圍安州，李希烈遣其甥劉戒虛將步騎八千救之。

translations.literal: Prince Cao Wang Gao sent his generals Yi Shen and Wang E to besiege Anzhou; Li Xilie sent his nephew Liu Jiexu with eight thousand infantry and cavalry to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cao Wang Gao sent his generals Yi Shen and Wang E to besiege Anzhou. Li Xilie sent his nephew Liu Jiexu with eight thousand foot and horse to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 皋遣別將李伯潛逆擊之於應山，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: Gao sent another general, Li Boqian, to intercept them at Yingshan and took more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent another general, Li Boqian, to intercept them at Yingshan and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 生擒戒虛，徇於城下，安州遂降。

translations.literal: Jiexu was captured alive and displayed below the walls; Anzhou then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jiexu was captured alive and paraded below the walls, and Anzhou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 以伊慎為安州刺史，又擊希烈將康叔夜於厲鄉，走之。

translations.literal: Yi Shen was made prefect of Anzhou, and again struck Li Xilie's general Kang Shuye at Lixiang and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Shen was appointed prefect of Anzhou and again struck Li Xilie's general Kang Shuye at Lixiang, driving him off.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，孔巢父至河中，李懷光素服待罪，巢父不之止。

translations.literal: On dinghai day Kong Chaofu reached Hezhong. Li Huaiguang wore plain dress awaiting judgment; Chaofu did not stop him.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day Kong Chaofu reached Hezhong. Li Huaiguang wore plain dress to await judgment, and Chaofu did not stop him.

sentences.zh: 懷光左右多胡人，皆歎曰：「太尉無官矣！」

translations.literal: Many of Huaiguang's attendants were men of the Hu tribes; they all sighed: "The Grand Marshal has lost his office!"
translations.idiomatic: Many of Huaiguang's attendants were men of the Hu tribes. They all sighed: "The Grand Marshal has lost his office!"

sentences.zh: 巢父又宣言於眾曰：「軍中誰可代太尉領軍者？」

translations.literal: Chaofu further announced to the assembly: "Who in the army can take the Grand Marshal's place and command the troops?"
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu then announced to the assembly: "Who in the army can take the Grand Marshal's place and command the troops?"

sentences.zh: 於是懷光左右發怒喧噪。

translations.literal: At this Huaiguang's attendants flared up in anger and clamor.
translations.idiomatic: At this Huaiguang's attendants erupted in anger and uproar.

sentences.zh: 宣詔未畢，眾殺巢父及中使啖守盈，懷光亦不之止，復治兵為拒守之備。

translations.literal: Before the edict was fully read, the crowd killed Chaofu and the eunuch envoy Tan Shouying. Huaiguang did not stop them either, and again readied his troops for defensive resistance.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict had been fully read, the crowd killed Chaofu and the eunuch envoy Tan Shouying. Huaiguang did not stop them and again readied his troops for defense.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，赦天下。

translations.literal: On xinmao day there was a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 初，肅宗在靈武，上為奉節王，學文於李泌。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Suzong was at Lingwu, the present emperor was Prince of Fengjie and studied letters under Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Suzong was at Lingwu, the present emperor was Prince of Fengjie and studied under Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 代宗之世，泌居蓬萊書院，上為太子，亦與之遊。

translations.literal: In Emperor Daizong's reign Mi lived at Penglai Academy; when the present emperor was crown prince, he also kept company with Mi.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Daizong's reign Mi lived at Penglai Academy, and when the present emperor was crown prince he kept company with him as well.

sentences.zh: 及上在興元，泌為杭州刺史，上急詔征之，與睦州刺史杜亞俱詣行在。

translations.literal: When the emperor was at Xingyuan, Mi was prefect of Hangzhou; the emperor urgently summoned him by edict, and Mi came to the imperial camp together with Du Ya, prefect of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at Xingyuan, Mi was prefect of Hangzhou. The emperor urgently summoned him by edict, and Mi came to the imperial camp together with Du Ya, prefect of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以泌為左散騎常侍，亞為刑部侍郎，命泌日直西省以候對，朝野皆屬目附之。

translations.literal: On yiwei day, Mi was made Left Master of Regular Attendance and Ya was made Vice Minister of Justice; Mi was ordered to attend daily at the West Department to await imperial questions, and court and country alike turned their eyes to him with expectation.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day Mi was made left master of regular attendance and Ya vice minister of justice. Mi was ordered to attend daily at the West Department to await the emperor's questions, and all court and country turned their eyes to him with expectation.

sentences.zh: 上問泌：「河中密邇京城，朔方兵素稱精銳，如達奚小俊等皆萬人敵，朕晝夕憂之，奈何？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Mi: "Hezhong lies close to the capital; the Shuofang troops are famed for sharp prowess; men like Daxi Xiaojun are each a match for ten thousand—day and night I worry over this. What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Mi: "Hezhong lies close to the capital, and the Shuofang troops are famed for their prowess. Men like Daxi Xiaojun are each a match for ten thousand. Day and night I worry over this. What is to be done?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「天下事甚有可憂者，若惟河中，不足憂也。

translations.literal: He replied: "There are many things in the realm truly worth worry; if it is only Hezhong, it is not worth worrying over.
translations.idiomatic: Mi replied: "There are matters throughout the realm far more worrisome than this. Hezhong alone is nothing to fret over.

sentences.zh: 夫料敵者，料將不料兵。

translations.literal: In gauging the enemy, one gauges the general, not the troops.
translations.idiomatic: When sizing up an enemy, weigh the commander—not the ranks.

sentences.zh: 今懷光，將也；

translations.literal: Now Huai Guang is the general;
translations.idiomatic: Huai Guang is the general;

sentences.zh: 小俊之徒乃兵耳，何足為意！

translations.literal: men like Xiaojun are merely soldiers—what need to take them to heart!
translations.idiomatic: men like Xiaojun are merely troops. What is there to worry about?

sentences.zh: 懷光既解奉天之圍，視朱泚垂亡之虜不能取，乃與之連和，使李晟得取以為功。

translations.literal: Huai Guang, having lifted the siege of Fengtian, saw the nearly perishing captive Zhu Ci yet could not seize him, then allied with him, allowing Li Sheng to capture him and claim the merit.
translations.idiomatic: Having broken the siege of Fengtian, Huai Guang watched Zhu Ci's broken forces slip from his grasp—and then made common cause with the rebel, allowing Li Sheng to win the credit for the capture.

sentences.zh: 今陛下已還宮闕，懷光不束身歸罪，乃虐殺使臣，鼠伏河中，如夢魘之人耳！

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has returned to the palace; Huai Guang has not bound himself to submit and accept guilt, but instead cruelly killed envoys and crouches like a rat in Hezhong—no more than a man gripped by nightmare!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has returned to the palace, yet Huai Guang will not surrender and face judgment. He murders imperial envoys and skulks in Hezhong like a rat—a man living in a nightmare, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 但恐不日為帳下所梟，使諸將無以藉手也。」

translations.literal: Only I fear he will before long be beheaded by those under his tent, leaving the generals nothing to work with."
translations.idiomatic: I only fear his own officers will behead him ere long, leaving our generals no enemy to strike."

sentences.zh: 初，上發吐蕃以討朱泚。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had mobilized the Tibetans to attack Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had mobilized Tibetan forces against Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 許成功以伊西、北庭之地與之。

translations.literal: He promised that upon success he would give them the lands of Yixi and Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: He had promised them the Yixi and Beiting territories once victory was won.

sentences.zh: 及泚誅，吐蕃來求地，上欲召兩鎮節度使郭昕、李元忠還朝，以其地與之。

translations.literal: When Ci was executed, the Tibetans came to demand the land; the emperor wished to recall the military commissioners of the two commands, Guo Xin and Li Yuanzhong, to court and give them the land.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Ci's death the Tibetans came to claim the promised lands. The emperor intended to recall the commissioners of the two frontier commands—Guo Xin and Li Yuanzhong—and cede the territories to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 李泌曰：「安西、北庭，人性驍悍，控制西域五十七國及十姓突厥，又分吐蕃之勢，使不得並兵東侵，奈何拱手與之！

translations.literal: Li Mi said: "Anxi and Beiting—the people there are fierce and hardy; they control fifty-seven states of the Western Regions and the Ten Surname Turks, and they also divide Tibetan strength so that Tibet cannot combine its armies for eastern invasion—how can we simply hand it over with clasped hands!
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi said: "The garrisons of Anxi and Beiting hold fierce, hardy peoples who control fifty-seven states of the Western Regions and the Ten Surname Turks. They tie down Tibetan power and keep Tibet from massing armies for an eastern invasion. How can we simply surrender those positions?

sentences.zh: 且兩鎮之人，勢孤地遠，盡忠竭力，為國家固守近二十年，誠可哀憐。

translations.literal: Moreover, the people of the two commands, isolated in strength and distant in terrain, have exhausted loyalty and strength, holding fast for the state for nearly twenty years—it is truly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: These two commands stand alone and far from home. Their people have labored in loyalty for nearly twenty years to hold the frontier for the state. It is a cause for genuine pity.

sentences.zh: 一旦棄之以與戎狄，彼其心必深怨中國，它日從吐蕃入寇，如報私仇矣。

translations.literal: Once we abandon them and give them to the barbarians, their hearts will surely deeply resent China; another day they will follow the Tibetans in invasion, as though settling a private score.
translations.idiomatic: Abandon them to the barbarians and they will harbor deep resentment against the court. One day they will ride with the Tibetans against us—as if settling a personal score.

sentences.zh: 況日者吐蕃觀望不進，陰持兩端，大掠武功，受賂而去，何功之有！」

translations.literal: Moreover, lately the Tibetans watched and did not advance, secretly maintained both sides, greatly plundered Wugong, took bribes and departed—what merit was there!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the Tibetans recently dallied on the sidelines, played both sides, plundered Wugong on a vast scale, took bribes, and marched away. What service did they render?"

sentences.zh: 眾議亦以為然，上遂不與。

translations.literal: The assembled opinion also held likewise, and the emperor thereupon did not give the land.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers agreed, and the emperor declined to cede the territories.

sentences.zh: 李希烈聞李希倩伏誅，忿怒，八月，壬寅，遣中使至蔡州殺顏真卿。

translations.literal: Li Xilie, hearing that Li Xiqian had been executed in secret, was enraged; in the eighth month, on renyin day, he sent a palace envoy to Cai Prefecture to kill Yan Zhenqing.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie learned that Li Xiqian had been secretly executed, he flew into a rage. In the eighth month, on renyin day, he sent a palace envoy to Cai Prefecture to kill Yan Zhenqing.

sentences.zh: 中使曰：「有敕。」

translations.literal: The envoy said: "There is an imperial edict."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy announced: "By imperial edict."

sentences.zh: 真卿再拜。

translations.literal: Zhenqing bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 中使曰：「今賜卿死。」

translations.literal: The envoy said: "Now you are granted death."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said: "You are sentenced to death."

sentences.zh: 真卿曰：「老臣無狀，罪當死，不知使者幾日發長安？」

translations.literal: Zhenqing said: "This old minister is without merit, crime deserving death—I do not know on what day the envoy departed Chang'an?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing said: "This old minister has failed in his duty and deserves death. When did the envoy leave Chang'an?"

sentences.zh: 使者曰：「自大梁來，非長安也。」

translations.literal: The envoy said: "I came from Daliang—not from Chang'an."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy replied: "I came from Daliang—not from Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 真卿曰：「然則賊耳，何謂敕邪！」

translations.literal: Zhenqing said: "Then you are a rebel—what call this an edict!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing said: "Then you are a rebel. What right have you to speak of an imperial edict?"

sentences.zh: 遂縊殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they strangled and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They strangled him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 李晟以涇州倚邊，屢害軍帥，常為亂根，奏請往理不用命者，力田積粟以攘吐蕃。
