translations.literal: Li Sheng, because Jing Prefecture borders the frontier and repeatedly produced harm to army commanders, often serving as a root of disorder, memorialized requesting to go and deal with those who did not obey orders, to farm diligently and accumulate grain to repel the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng observed that Jing Prefecture, hard against the frontier, had repeatedly seen its commanders murdered and had long been a seedbed of rebellion. He memorialized the throne asking leave to go there, punish the disobedient, and push intensive farming and grain reserves to hold the Tibetans at bay.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以晟兼鳳翔、隴右節度等使及四鎮、北庭、涇原行營副元帥，進爵西平王。

translations.literal: On guimao day, Sheng was made concurrently commissioner of Fengxiang, Longyou, and related commands, as well as deputy commander-in-chief of the Four Commands, Beiting, and Jingyuan field headquarters, and advanced in rank to Prince of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day Li Sheng was appointed concurrent military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou and related commands, deputy commander-in-chief of the Four Commands, Beiting, and Jingyuan field headquarters, and ennobled as Prince of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 時李楚琳入朝，晟請與俱至鳳翔斬之，以懲逆亂。

translations.literal: At the time Li Chulin was attending court; Sheng requested to go with him to Fengxiang and behead him, to punish rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chulin was then at court. Sheng asked permission to escort him to Fengxiang and execute him as a warning against rebellion.

sentences.zh: 上以新復京師，務安反仄，不許。

translations.literal: The emperor, having newly recovered the capital, was set on settling discontent, and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, intent on pacifying the realm after the recovery of the capital, refused.

sentences.zh: 先是，上命渾瑊、駱元光討李懷光軍於同州，懷光遣其將徐庭光以精卒六千軍於長春宮以拒之，瑊等數為所敗，不能進。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had ordered Hun Jian and Luo Yuanguang to attack Li Huai Guang's army at Tong Prefecture; Huai Guang sent his general Xu Tingguang with six thousand elite troops to encamp at Changchun Palace to resist them; Jian and the others were repeatedly defeated and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had ordered Hun Jian and Luo Yuanguang to attack Li Huai Guang's forces at Tong Prefecture. Huai Guang sent his general Xu Tingguang with six thousand elite troops to hold Changchun Palace. Hun Jian's forces were driven back again and again and could not advance.

sentences.zh: 時度支用度不給，議者多請赦懷光，上不許。

translations.literal: At the time the treasury's expenditures could not be met; many in council pleaded to pardon Huai Guang, and the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury could not meet its obligations. Many at court urged pardoning Huai Guang, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 李懷光遣其妹婿要廷珍守晉州，牙將毛朝易文守隰州，鄭抗守慈州，馬燧皆遣人說下之。

translations.literal: Li Huai Guang sent his brother-in-law Yao Tingzhen to hold Jin Prefecture, staff officer Mao Chao Yiwen to hold Xi Prefecture, and Zheng Kang to hold Ci Prefecture; Ma Sui all sent men to persuade them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai Guang had his brother-in-law Yao Tingzhen hold Jin Prefecture, staff officer Mao Chao Yiwen hold Xi Prefecture, and Zheng Kang hold Ci Prefecture. Ma Sui sent emissaries to each and persuaded them all to defect.

sentences.zh: 上乃加渾瑊河中、絳州節度使，充河中、同華、陝虢行營副元帥，加馬燧奉誠軍、晉、慈、隰節度使，充管內諸軍行營副元帥，與鎮國節度使駱元光、鄜坊節度使唐朝臣合兵討懷光。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon promoted Hun Jian to military commissioner of Hezhong and Jiang Prefecture, made him deputy commander-in-chief of the Hezhong, Tonghua, and Shan-Guo field headquarters, promoted Ma Sui to military commissioner of the Fengcheng Army and Jin, Ci, and Xi Prefectures, made him deputy commander-in-chief of all armies within his jurisdiction, and together with Zhenguo military commissioner Luo Yuanguang and Yanfang military commissioner Tang Chaochen combined forces to attack Huai Guang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then appointed Hun Jian military commissioner of Hezhong and Jiang Prefecture and deputy commander-in-chief of the Hezhong, Tonghua, and Shan-Guo field headquarters; appointed Ma Sui military commissioner of the Fengcheng Army and of Jin, Ci, and Xi Prefectures and deputy commander-in-chief of all armies under his command; and ordered them to join Zhenguo commissioner Luo Yuanguang and Yanfang commissioner Tang Chaochen in a combined campaign against Huai Guang.

sentences.zh: 初，王武俊急攻康日知於趙州，馬燧奏請詔武俊與李抱真同擊朱滔，以深、趙隸武俊，改日知為晉、慈、隰節度使，上從之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Wujun was pressing Kang Rizhi hard at Zhao Prefecture; Ma Sui memorialized requesting an edict for Wujun and Li Baozhen to jointly attack Zhu Tao, assign Shen and Zhao to Wujun, and change Rizhi to military commissioner of Jin, Ci, and Xi Prefectures; the emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Wujun had been pressing Kang Rizhi hard at Zhao Prefecture. Ma Sui memorialized the throne asking that Wujun and Li Baozhen be ordered to attack Zhu Tao jointly, that Shen and Zhao be assigned to Wujun, and that Rizhi be transferred to command Jin, Ci, and Xi Prefectures. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 日知未至而三州降燧，故上使燧兼領之。

translations.literal: Rizhi had not yet arrived when the three prefectures surrendered to Sui, so the emperor had Sui hold them concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi had not yet arrived when all three prefectures surrendered to Ma Sui, so the emperor had Sui hold them in the interim.

sentences.zh: 燧表讓三州於日知，且言因降而授，恐後有功者，踵以為常，上嘉而許之。

translations.literal: Sui memorialized ceding the three prefectures to Rizhi, and said that granting territory because of surrender feared that later men of merit would follow suit as a precedent; the emperor praised this and permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui memorialized offering the three prefectures back to Rizhi, arguing that rewarding surrender with territory would invite future commanders to treat defection as a routine path to reward. The emperor praised his integrity and agreed.

sentences.zh: 燧遣使迎日知。

translations.literal: Sui sent an envoy to welcome Rizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui sent an envoy to escort Rizhi to his new command.

sentences.zh: 既至，籍府庫而歸之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Sui inventoried the treasury and returned it to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Rizhi arrived, Ma Sui inventoried the prefectural treasury and handed everything over intact.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以鳳翔節度使李楚琳為左金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: On jiachen day, Fengxiang military commissioner Li Chulin was made Left Great General of the Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Li Chulin, military commissioner of Fengxiang, was appointed left great general of the Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 丙午，加渾瑊朔方行營元帥。

translations.literal: On bingwu day, Hun Jian was additionally made commander-in-chief of the Shuofang field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day Hun Jian was additionally appointed commander-in-chief of the Shuofang field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 李晟至鳳翔，治殺張鎰之罪，斬裨將王斌等十餘人。

translations.literal: Li Sheng arrived at Fengxiang, prosecuted the crime of killing Zhang Yin, and beheaded assistant generals Wang Bin and more than ten others.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Sheng reached Fengxiang he prosecuted those responsible for Zhang Yin's murder and beheaded more than ten officers, including assistant general Wang Bin.

sentences.zh: 朱滔為王武俊所攻，殆不能軍，上表待罪。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao, attacked by Wang Wujun, could barely maintain an army and submitted a memorial accepting guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao, battered by Wang Wujun's attacks, could barely keep his army together and submitted a memorial accepting blame.

sentences.zh: 癸未，馬燧將步騎三萬攻絳州。

translations.literal: On guiwei day, Ma Sui led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day Ma Sui marched thirty thousand infantry and cavalry against Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 度支以李懷光所部將士數萬與懷光同反，不給冬衣，上曰：「朔方軍累代忠義，今為懷光所制耳，將士何罪！」

translations.literal: The treasury, because the several tens of thousands of officers and soldiers under Li Huai Guang had rebelled with him, withheld winter clothing; the emperor said: "The Shuofang army has been loyal for generations; now it is merely controlled by Huai Guang—what crime have the soldiers committed!"
translations.idiomatic: Because the tens of thousands of troops under Li Huai Guang had rebelled with him, the treasury withheld their winter clothing. The emperor said: "The Shuofang army has been loyal for generations. Huai Guang alone holds them in his grip. What crime have the rank and file committed?

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，已亥，詔：「朔方及諸軍在懷光所者，冬衣及賞錢皆當別貯，俟道路稍通，即時給之。」

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on jihai day, an edict proclaimed: "For the Shuofang army and all other forces with Huai Guang, winter clothing and reward money shall all be set aside separately; once the roads are somewhat open, they shall be issued at once."
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on jihai day, an edict was issued: "Winter clothing and reward pay for the Shuofang army and all other troops still with Huai Guang shall be set aside separately and issued the moment the roads are passable again."

sentences.zh: 李勉累表乞自貶，辛丑，罷勉都統、節度使，其檢校司徒、同平章事如故。

translations.literal: Li Mian repeatedly memorialized begging to demote himself; on xinchou day Mian was removed as overall commander and military commissioner, while his honorary titles of Grand Preceptor and Co-equal with the Department of State Affairs remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian repeatedly memorialized asking to be demoted. On xinchou day he was stripped of his posts as overall commander and military commissioner, but retained his honorary titles of grand preceptor and co-equal with the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，李懷光將閻晏寇同州，官軍敗於沙苑。

translations.literal: On bingchen day, Li Huai Guang's general Yan Yan raided Tong Prefecture, and the government army was defeated at Shayuan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day Li Huai Guang's general Yan Yan raided Tong Prefecture, and the imperial army was routed at Shayuan.

sentences.zh: 詔征邠州之軍，韓游瑰將甲士六千赴之。

translations.literal: An edict mobilized the army of Bin Prefecture; Han Yougui led six thousand armored troops to the scene.
translations.idiomatic: An edict mobilized the Bin Prefecture army, and Han Yougui marched six thousand armored troops to reinforce the front.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，馬燧拔絳州，分兵取聞喜、萬泉、虞鄉、永樂、猗氏。

translations.literal: On yichou day, Ma Sui captured Jiang Prefecture and dispatched troops to take Wenxi, Wanquan, Yuxiang, Yongle, and Yishi.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day Ma Sui took Jiang Prefecture and sent detachments to seize Wenxi, Wanquan, Yuxiang, Yongle, and Yishi.

sentences.zh: 初，魚朝恩既誅，代宗不復使宦官典兵。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Yu Chaoen was executed, Emperor Daizong no longer employed eunuchs to command troops.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu Chaoen's execution, Emperor Daizong had ceased appointing eunuchs to command troops.

sentences.zh: 上即位，悉以禁兵委白志貞，志貞得罪，上復以宦官竇文場代之，從幸山南，兩軍稍集。

translations.literal: When the present emperor ascended the throne, he entrusted all the palace guard entirely to Bai Zhizhen; when Zhizhen fell from favor, the emperor again replaced him with the eunuch Dou Wenchang; accompanying the emperor to Shannan, the two armies gradually assembled.
translations.idiomatic: When the present emperor took the throne he entrusted the entire palace guard to Bai Zhizhen. After Zhizhen fell from favor the emperor replaced him with the eunuch Dou Wenchang. Dou accompanied the emperor to Shannan, and the two palace armies gradually reassembled.

sentences.zh: 上還長安，頗忌宿將握兵多者，稍稍罷之。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to Chang'an, he was rather wary of veteran generals who held large armies, and gradually removed them.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to Chang'an the emperor grew wary of veteran generals who commanded large armies and gradually stripped them of their commands.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以文場監神策軍左廂兵馬使，王希遷監石廂兵馬使，始令宦官分典禁旅。

translations.literal: On wuchen day, Wenchang was made overseer of the left wing of the Shence Army's horse and infantry, and Wang Xiqian overseer of the right wing; eunuchs were for the first time put in divided charge of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day Dou Wenchang was appointed overseer of the left wing of the Shence Army's horse and infantry and Wang Xiqian overseer of the right wing—the first time eunuchs were given divided command of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 閏月，丙子，以涇原節度使田希鑒為衛尉卿。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on bingzi day, Jingyuan military commissioner Tian Xijian was made Minister of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on bingzi day, Tian Xijian, military commissioner of Jingyuan, was appointed minister of the guard.

sentences.zh: 李晟初至鳳翔，希鑒遣使參候，晟謂使者曰：「涇州逼近吐蕃，萬一入寇，州兵能獨御之乎？

translations.literal: When Li Sheng had first arrived at Fengxiang, Xijian sent an envoy to pay his respects; Sheng said to the envoy: "Jing Prefecture presses close to Tibet; if Tibet should invade, can the prefectural troops repel them alone?
translations.idiomatic: When Li Sheng first reached Fengxiang, Tian Xijian sent an envoy to pay his respects. Sheng told the envoy: "Jing Prefecture lies hard against the Tibetan frontier. If the Tibetans should raid, can the local garrison hold them off alone?

sentences.zh: 欲遣兵防援，又未知田尚書意。」

translations.literal: I wish to send troops to garrison and support, but I do not yet know Minister Tian's intent."
translations.idiomatic: I would like to send troops to reinforce the prefecture, but I do not yet know what Minister Tian intends."

sentences.zh: 使者歸，以告希鑒，希鑒果請援兵，晟遣腹心將彭令英等戍涇州。

translations.literal: The envoy returned and reported this to Xijian; Xijian indeed requested reinforcing troops, and Sheng sent his trusted generals Peng Lingying and others to garrison Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy returned and relayed this, Tian Xijian promptly requested reinforcements. Sheng sent his trusted generals Peng Lingying and others to garrison Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 晟尋托巡邊詣涇州，希鑒出迎，晟與之並轡而入，道舊結歡。

translations.literal: Sheng soon pleaded a frontier inspection and went to Jing Prefecture; Xijian came out to welcome him, and Sheng entered riding side by side with him, speaking of old friendship and renewed goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng soon pleaded a frontier inspection and rode to Jing Prefecture. Tian Xijian came out to welcome him, and the two entered the city riding side by side, speaking warmly of old friendship.

sentences.zh: 希鑒妻李氏，以叔父事晟，晟謂之田郎。

translations.literal: Xijian's wife, Lady Li, treated Sheng as an uncle; Sheng called her husband Tian Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xijian's wife, Lady Li, treated Sheng as an uncle by marriage, and Sheng affectionately called her husband "Young Tian."

sentences.zh: 晟命具三日食，曰：「巡撫畢，即還鳳翔。」

translations.literal: Sheng ordered three days' provisions prepared and said: "Once the inspection is finished, I shall return at once to Fengxiang."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng ordered three days' rations prepared and said: "Once my inspection is done I shall return straightaway to Fengxiang."

sentences.zh: 希鑒不復疑。

translations.literal: Xijian no longer harbored suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xijian's suspicions were put to rest.

sentences.zh: 晟置宴，希鑒與將佐俱詣晟營。

translations.literal: Sheng set a banquet; Xijian and his officers all came to Sheng's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng hosted a banquet, and Tian Xijian and his officers all came to his camp.

sentences.zh: 晟伏甲於外廡，既食而飲，彭令英引涇州諸將下堂。

translations.literal: Sheng hid armored men in the outer corridor; after they had eaten and were drinking, Peng Lingying led the Jing Prefecture generals down from the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had armored men concealed in the outer corridor. After the meal, as wine was being served, Peng Lingying led the Jing Prefecture generals from the hall.

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「我與汝曹久別，各宜自言姓名。」

translations.literal: Sheng said: "I have long been parted from you all—each of you should speak your name."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said: "We have been long apart. Each of you—give your name."

sentences.zh: 於是得為亂者石奇等三十餘人，讓之曰：「汝曹屢為逆亂，殘害忠良，固天地所不容！」

translations.literal: Thereupon he identified more than thirty men who had joined in rebellion, including Shi Qi, and rebuked them, saying: "You all have repeatedly joined in rebellion and slaughtered the loyal and good—surely heaven and earth cannot tolerate you!"
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty men implicated in the rebellions—including Shi Qi—stepped forward. Sheng rebuked them: "You have again and again risen in rebellion and butchered the loyal. Heaven and earth themselves cannot abide such men!"

sentences.zh: 悉引出，斬之。

translations.literal: He had them all led out and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He had them all led out and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 希鑒尚在座，晟顧曰：「田郎亦不得無過，以親知之故，當使身首得完。」

translations.literal: Xijian was still seated; Sheng turned and said: "Young Tian, you too cannot be without fault; because of our kinship and friendship, I shall let you keep body and head intact."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xijian was still at table. Sheng turned to him and said: "Young Tian, you are not without fault—but because we are kin by marriage, I shall let you die whole."

sentences.zh: 希鑒曰：「唯。」

translations.literal: Xijian said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xijian said only: "Yes."

sentences.zh: 遂引出，縊殺之，並其子萼。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was led out and strangled, together with his son E.
translations.idiomatic: He was led out and strangled, together with his son E.

sentences.zh: 晟入其營，諭以誅希鑒之意，眾股慄，無敢動者。

translations.literal: Sheng entered their camp and announced the reason for executing Xijian; the masses trembled in their thighs and none dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng entered the Jing Prefecture camp and explained why Tian Xijian had been executed. The troops trembled with fear and none dared move.

sentences.zh: 李希烈遣其將翟崇暉悉眾圍陳州，久之，不克。

translations.literal: Li Xilie sent his general Zhai Chonghui with his entire force to besiege Chen Prefecture; after a long time he could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie sent his general Zhai Chonghui with the full rebel host to besiege Chen Prefecture, but after a long siege the city still held.

sentences.zh: 李澄知大梁兵少，不能制滑州，遂焚希烈所授旌節，誓眾歸國。

translations.literal: Li Cheng, knowing that Daliang had few troops and could not control Hua Prefecture, thereupon burned the banner and credentials Xilie had granted him and swore the host to return to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng saw that Daliang's garrison was too thin to hold Hua Prefecture. He burned the banner and credentials Li Xilie had granted him and rallied his troops to swear loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以澄為汴滑節度使。

translations.literal: On jiawu day, Cheng was made military commissioner of Bian and Hua Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day Li Cheng was appointed military commissioner of Bian and Hua Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 宋亳節度使劉洽遣馬步都虞候劉昌與隴右、幽州行營節度使曲環等將兵三萬救陳州，十一月，癸卯，敗翟崇暉於州西，斬首三萬五千級，擒崇暉以獻。

translations.literal: Song-Bo military commissioner Liu Qia sent cavalry and infantry chief adjutant Liu Chang together with Longyou and Youzhou field headquarters commissioner Qu Huan and others to lead thirty thousand troops to relieve Chen Prefecture; in the eleventh month, on guimao day, they defeated Zhai Chonghui west of the prefecture, beheaded thirty-five thousand, and captured Chonghui to present as trophy.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qia, military commissioner of Song and Bo, sent his chief adjutant Liu Chang together with Qu Huan, commissioner of the Longyou and Youzhou field headquarters, and others at the head of thirty thousand troops to relieve Chen Prefecture. In the eleventh month, on guimao day, they routed Zhai Chonghui west of the city, took thirty-five thousand heads, and captured Chonghui alive.

sentences.zh: 乘勝進攻汴州，李希烈懼，奔歸蔡州。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory, they advanced to attack Bian Prefecture; Xilie was afraid and fled back to Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The victors pressed on toward Bian Prefecture. Li Xilie, terrified, fled back to Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李澄引兵趣汴州，至城北，恇怯不敢進。

translations.literal: Li Cheng led troops toward Bian Prefecture; when he reached the north of the city he was timid and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng marched on Bian Prefecture but halted at the north wall, too fearful to enter.

sentences.zh: 劉洽兵至成東。

translations.literal: Liu Qia's army reached Chengdong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qia's army reached Chengdong.

sentences.zh: 戊午，李希烈守將田懷珍開門納之。

translations.literal: On wuwu day, Li Xilie's defending general Tian Huaizhen opened the gates and admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day Li Xilie's garrison commander Tian Huaizhen opened the gates and welcomed the imperial army in.

sentences.zh: 明日，澄入，捨於浚儀。

translations.literal: The next day Cheng entered and lodged at Junyi.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Li Cheng entered the city and took up quarters at Junyi.

sentences.zh: 兩軍之士，日有忿鬩。

translations.literal: The soldiers of the two armies daily had angry brawls.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers of the two armies brawled with one another day after day.

sentences.zh: 會希烈鄭州守將孫液降於澄，澄引兵屯鄭州。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Xilie's Zheng Prefecture defending general Sun Ye surrendered to Cheng; Cheng led troops to encamp at Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie's Zheng Prefecture commander Sun Ye defected to Li Cheng, Cheng marched his troops to occupy Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔以都統司馬寶鼎薛玨為汴州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed overall command staff officer Baoding Xue Jue as prefect of Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Xue Jue of Baoding, staff officer to the overall commander, prefect of Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李勉至長安，素服待罪。

translations.literal: Li Mian arrived at Chang'an and, in plain white garments, awaited judgment for his fault.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian reached Chang'an dressed in plain white and waited to accept punishment.

sentences.zh: 議者多以「勉失守大梁，不應尚為相。」

translations.literal: Many in council held that "Mian lost Daliang and ought not still to serve as chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Many at court argued that "Mian lost Daliang and should no longer serve as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 李泌言於上曰：「李勉公忠雅正，而用兵非其所長。

translations.literal: Li Mi said to the emperor: "Li Mian is public-spirited, loyal, refined, and upright, but commanding troops is not his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi told the emperor: "Li Mian is loyal, upright, and principled, but warfare is not his strength.

sentences.zh: 乃大梁不守，將士棄妻子而從之者殆二萬人，足以見其得眾心矣。

translations.literal: Yet when Daliang could not be held, officers and soldiers who abandoned wives and children to follow him numbered nearly twenty thousand—enough to show that he had won the hearts of the masses.
translations.idiomatic: When Daliang fell, nearly twenty thousand soldiers abandoned their wives and children to follow him—that alone shows how deeply they trusted him.

sentences.zh: 且劉洽出勉麾下，勉至睢陽，悉舉其眾以授之，卒平大梁，亦勉之功也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Liu Qia came from under Mian's command; when Mian reached Suiyang he turned over his entire force to him, and in the end Daliang was pacified—this too was Mian's merit."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qia served under Mian. When Mian reached Suiyang he turned his entire force over to Liu Qia, who in the end recovered Daliang—that victory is Mian's as well."

sentences.zh: 上乃命勉復其位。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon ordered Mian restored to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Li Mian restored to office.

sentences.zh: 議者又言：「韓滉聞鑾輿在外，聚兵修石頭城，陰蓄異志。」

translations.literal: Counselors spoke again: "Han Huang, hearing that the imperial carriage was abroad, gathered troops and repaired Shitou City, secretly harboring a different intent."
translations.idiomatic: Critics spoke again: "When Han Huang learned the emperor had fled the capital, he gathered troops and fortified Shitou City—clear evidence of secret disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 上疑之，以問李泌，對曰：「滉公忠清儉，自車駕在外，滉貢獻不絕。

translations.literal: The emperor was suspicious and asked Li Mi; he replied: "Huang is public-spirited, loyal, pure, and frugal; from the time the imperial carriage was abroad, Huang's tribute offerings never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was troubled and asked Li Mi. Mi replied: "Han Huang is loyal, upright, and austere. From the day Your Majesty left the capital his tribute shipments never stopped.

sentences.zh: 且鎮撫江東十五州，盜賊不起，皆滉之力也。

translations.literal: Moreover, in pacifying the fifteen prefectures east of the Yangzi, bandits did not rise—all this was Huang's power at work.
translations.idiomatic: He has kept peace across fifteen prefectures east of the Yangzi without a single bandit rising. That is Han Huang's doing.

sentences.zh: 所以修石頭城者，滉見中原板蕩，謂陛下將有永嘉之行，為迎扈之備耳。

translations.literal: The reason he repaired Shitou City was that Huang saw the Central Plain in turmoil and believed Your Majesty would make a Yongjia journey, preparing only to welcome and escort the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified Shitou City because he saw the heartland in chaos and believed Your Majesty might need a refuge like the Yongjia flight—he was preparing to receive and protect the throne, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 此乃人臣忠篤之慮，奈何更以為罪乎！

translations.literal: This is merely a loyal and earnest concern of a subject—how can it further be made a crime!
translations.idiomatic: That is the foresight of a loyal subject. How can it be turned into a crime?

sentences.zh: 滉性剛嚴，不附權貴，故多謗毀，願陛下察之，臣敢保其無它。」

translations.literal: Huang's nature is stern and severe; he does not attach himself to the powerful and noble, hence there is much slander—Your Majesty, I beg you to examine this; I dare guarantee he has no other intent."
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang is stern by nature and refuses to court the powerful, so he has many enemies. I beg Your Majesty to look closely—I will stake my life that he harbors no disloyalty."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「外議洶洶，章奏如麻，卿弗聞乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Outside opinion is in uproar; memorials pile up like hemp—have you not heard?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The talk outside court is a roar, and memorials pile up like sheaves of hemp. Have you not heard any of it?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣固聞之。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant has indeed heard it.
translations.idiomatic: Mi replied: "I have heard it, of course.

sentences.zh: 其子皋為考功員外郎，今不敢歸省其親，正以謗語沸騰故也。」

translations.literal: His son Gao is an outer office director in the Ministry of Personnel; he now does not dare return home to visit his parent, precisely because slander is boiling over."
translations.idiomatic: His son Gao serves as an outer office director in the Ministry of Personnel. He dares not even visit his father at home—such is the fury of the slander."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「其子猶懼如此，卿奈何保之？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If even his son fears this much, how can you guarantee him?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If even his son is this afraid, how can you vouch for him?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「滉之用心，臣知之至熟。

translations.literal: He replied: "Huang's intent—I know it most thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Mi replied: "I know Han Huang's heart better than anyone.

sentences.zh: 願上章明其無它，乞宣示中書，使朝眾皆知之。」

translations.literal: I wish to memorialize the throne clarifying that he has no other intent, and beg that it be proclaimed to the Secretariat so that the court assembly may all know it."
translations.idiomatic: Let me memorialize the throne declaring his innocence and ask that the edict be circulated through the Secretariat so all court may know the truth."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕方欲用卿，人亦何易可保！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I am just about to employ you—how easily can any man be guaranteed!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I am about to rely on you myself. No man's loyalty is so easily guaranteed!

sentences.zh: 慎勿違眾，恐並為卿累也。」

translations.literal: Be careful not to go against the multitude—I fear it will become a burden upon you as well."
translations.idiomatic: Take care not to defy public opinion—you may bring ruin upon yourself as well."

sentences.zh: 泌退，遂上章，請以百口保滉。

translations.literal: Mi withdrew and at once submitted a memorial, asking to guarantee Huang with the lives of a hundred mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Mi withdrew—and immediately submitted a memorial pledging the lives of his entire household in Han Huang's defense.

sentences.zh: 它日，上謂泌曰：「卿竟上章，已為卿留中。

translations.literal: Another day the emperor said to Mi: "You did submit a memorial after all; I have held it within for you.
translations.idiomatic: Some days later the emperor said to Li Mi: "You submitted that memorial after all. I have kept it on my desk and taken no action—for your sake.

sentences.zh: 雖知卿與滉親舊，豈得不自愛其身乎！」

translations.literal: Although I know you and Huang are kin and old friends, how can you fail to cherish your own person!"
translations.idiomatic: I know you and Han Huang are old friends—but should you not have more regard for your own safety!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣豈肯私於親舊以負陛下！

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant—how could I favor kin and old friends and fail Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: Mi replied: "How could I put personal ties ahead of my duty to Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 顧滉實無異心，臣之上章，以為朝廷，非為身也。」

translations.literal: But Huang truly has no other intent; my submitting the memorial was for the court, not for myself."
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang truly has no treacherous intent. I spoke up for the sake of the dynasty—not for myself."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「如何其為朝廷？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In what way was it for the court?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "How was that for the good of the court?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「今天下旱、蝗，關中米斗千錢，倉廩耗竭，而江東豐稔。

translations.literal: He replied: "Now the realm suffers drought and locusts; in Guanzhong rice is a thousand cash per dou, granaries are exhausted, yet the lands east of the Jiang are bountiful.
translations.idiomatic: Mi answered: "The realm suffers drought and locusts. In Guanzhong a dou of rice costs a thousand cash and the granaries are empty—yet the lands east of the Yangtze have had a fine harvest.

sentences.zh: 願陛下早下臣章以解朝眾之惑，面諭韓皋使之歸覲，令滉感謝無自疑之心，速運糧儲，豈非為朝廷邪？」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would early promulgate my memorial to dispel the court's bewilderment, instruct Han Gao face to face to return and pay homage, cause Huang to feel gratitude and have no heart to doubt himself, and speed the transport of grain stores—is this not for the court?"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would publish my memorial and clear the court's suspicions; if you would summon Han Gao home and tell him face to face that his father is cleared; if Han Huang could be grateful rather than fearful and rush grain north—would that not serve the dynasty?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Well said!

sentences.zh: 朕深諭之矣。」

translations.literal: I have thoroughly understood it."
translations.idiomatic: I understand you fully."

sentences.zh: 即下泌章，令韓皋謁告歸覲，面賜緋衣，諭以「卿父比有謗言，朕今知其所以，釋然不覆信矣。」

translations.literal: At once he promulgated Mi's memorial, ordered Han Gao to take leave and return home, face to face bestowed scarlet robes, and instructed him: "Your father lately had slander spoken against him; I now know the reason and am relieved—I shall not believe such talk again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor published Mi's memorial, granted Han Gao leave to visit home, and personally gave him scarlet robes. "Your father has been much slandered," he said. "I now understand why, and I shall not believe such rumors again.

sentences.zh: 因言：「關中乏糧，歸語卿父，宜速致之。」

translations.literal: He then said: "Guanzhong lacks grain; return and tell your father he should speedily deliver it."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Guanzhong is starving for grain. Tell your father to send supplies at once.

sentences.zh: 皋至潤州，滉感悅流涕，即日，自臨水濱發米百萬斛，聽皋留五日即還朝。

translations.literal: When Gao reached Runzhou, Huang was moved and wept with joy; that very day, he personally went to the riverbank and dispatched a million hu of rice, allowing Gao to stay five days and then return to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gao reached Runzhou, Han Huang wept with gratitude. That same day Huang went to the waterfront himself and dispatched a million hu of grain. Gao was permitted five days with his family before returning to court.

sentences.zh: 皋別其母，啼聲聞於外。

translations.literal: When Gao took leave of his mother, the sound of weeping was heard outside.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao bid farewell to his mother, his weeping could be heard outside the room.

sentences.zh: 滉怒，召出，撻之，自送至江上，冒風濤而遣之。

translations.literal: Huang grew angry, summoned him out, flogged him, personally escorted him to the river, and sent him off through wind and waves.
translations.idiomatic: Huang flew into a rage, had him brought out and flogged, then escorted him to the river himself and sent him off through wind and waves.

sentences.zh: 既而陳少游聞滉貢米，亦貢二十萬斛。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Chen Shaoyou, hearing that Huang had presented tribute grain, also presented two hundred thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Shaoyou learned that Han Huang had sent tribute grain, he contributed two hundred thousand hu as well.

sentences.zh: 上謂李泌曰：「韓滉乃能化陳少游亦貢米矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Li Mi: "Han Huang has even been able to transform Chen Shaoyou into presenting tribute grain!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Li Mi: "Han Huang has even won over Chen Shaoyou—look, he sent grain too!

sentences.zh: 對曰：「豈惟少游，諸道將爭入貢矣！」

translations.literal: He replied: "It is not only Shaoyou—all the circuit commissioners will vie to enter tribute!"
translations.idiomatic: Mi replied: "It will not stop with Shaoyou. Every circuit in the empire will rush to send tribute!"

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書、同平章事蕭復奉使自江、淮還，與李勉、盧翰、劉從一俱見上。

translations.literal: Xiao Fu, Minister of Personnel and Concurrent Regular Attendant-in-Chief, returning from a mission from the Jiang and Huai regions, together with Li Mian, Lu Han, and Liu Congyi, all saw the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fu, Minister of Personnel and chief minister, had returned from a mission to the Jiang-Huai region. He appeared before the emperor together with Li Mian, Lu Han, and Liu Congyi.

sentences.zh: 勉等退，復獨留，言於上曰：「陳少游任兼將相，首敗臣節，韋皋幕府下僚，獨建忠義，請以皋代少游鎮淮南，使善惡著明。

translations.literal: When Mian and the others withdrew, Fu alone remained and said to the emperor: "Chen Shaoyou held posts combining general and minister; he was first to ruin the integrity of a subject. Wei Gao was a low officer in a military staff, yet alone established loyalty and righteousness—I ask that Gao replace Shaoyou to hold Huainan, so that good and evil may be made clear.
translations.idiomatic: After the others withdrew, Xiao Fu stayed behind. "Chen Shaoyou held both civil and military rank yet was the first to betray the throne," he said. "Wei Gao was a junior staff officer who alone stood firm. I ask that Gao replace Shaoyou as military governor of Huainan, so reward and punishment are plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋遣中使馬欽緒揖劉從一附耳語而去。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he sent the palace envoy Ma Qinxu to bow to Liu Congyi, speak into his ear, and depart.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the palace envoy Ma Qinxu was sent to Liu Congyi. He bowed, whispered in his ear, and left.

sentences.zh: 諸相還閤。

translations.literal: The chief ministers returned to the privy office.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers returned to the privy council chamber.

sentences.zh: 從一詣復曰：「欽緒宣旨，令從一與公議朝來所言事，即奏行之，勿令李、盧知。

translations.literal: Congyi went to Fu and said: "Qinxu announced the imperial will: Congyi and you are to discuss this morning's matter and immediately memorialize and carry it out—do not let Li and Lu know.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congyi sought out Xiao Fu. "Ma Qinxu conveyed the emperor's order," he said. "You and I are to discuss this morning's proposal, memorialize it at once, and execute it—without informing Li Mian or Lu Han.

sentences.zh: 敢問何事也？」

translations.literal: I venture to ask—what is the matter?"
translations.idiomatic: May I ask what it concerns?

sentences.zh: 復曰：「唐、虞黜陟，岳牧僉諧。

translations.literal: Fu said: "Under Tang and Yu, dismissal and promotion—the mountain lords all agreed in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fu said: "Even under the sage kings Yao and Shun, dismissals and promotions were debated openly among the regional lords.

sentences.zh: 爵人於朝，與士共之。

translations.literal: Bestowing ranks upon men in court was shared with the gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Bestowing rank at court was a matter debated with all the ministers.

sentences.zh: 使李、盧不堪為相，則罷之。

translations.literal: If Li and Lu are unfit to serve as chief ministers, then dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: If Li Mian and Lu Han are unfit to serve, dismiss them.

sentences.zh: 既在相位，朝廷政事，安得不與之同議而獨隱此一事乎！

translations.literal: Since they already hold the chief-ministerial rank, how can court affairs not be jointly deliberated with them while this one matter alone is concealed!
translations.idiomatic: But if they remain in office, how can we deliberate on state affairs without them while concealing this one decision!

sentences.zh: 此最當今之大弊，朝來主上已有斯言，復已面陳其不可，不謂聖意尚爾。

translations.literal: This is the greatest fault of the present age. This morning the sovereign already had such words; Fu had already stated face to face that it was impermissible—I did not expect the sagely intent still to be thus.
translations.idiomatic: This is the worst failing of our court. This morning the emperor spoke of doing exactly that, and I told him to his face it was wrong. I never thought he would still insist.

sentences.zh: 復不惜與公奏行之，但恐浸以成俗，未敢以告。」

translations.literal: Fu does not begrudge memorizing and carrying it out with you, but I fear it will gradually become custom—I did not dare tell you."
translations.idiomatic: I would not refuse to carry out your order—but I fear it will become habit, and that is why I could not disclose the matter.

sentences.zh: 竟不以事語從一。

translations.literal: In the end he did not tell Congyi the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he never told Liu Congyi what the proposal was.

sentences.zh: 從一奏之，上愈不悅，復乃上表辭位，乙丑，罷為左庶子。

translations.literal: Congyi memorialized about it; the emperor grew still more displeased. Fu then submitted a memorial resigning his post. On yichou he was removed and made Left Sub-Protector of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congyi reported the exchange anyway. The emperor's displeasure deepened. Xiao Fu submitted his resignation. On yichou day he was dismissed and made tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 劉洽克汴州，得《李希烈起居注》，云「某月日，陳少游上表歸順。」

translations.literal: Liu Qia captured Bianzhou and obtained Li Xilie's Daily Record, which stated: "On such-and-such month and day, Chen Shaoyou submitted a memorial submitting allegiance."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Qia took Bianzhou he found Li Xilie's daily record, which noted that on a certain date Chen Shaoyou had submitted a memorial pledging allegiance to the rebel.

sentences.zh: 少游聞之慚懼，發疾，十二月，乙亥，薨。

translations.literal: When Shaoyou heard this he was ashamed and afraid; illness seized him. In the twelfth month, on yihai, he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyou learned of this he was stricken with shame and fear. He fell ill and died in the twelfth month, on yihai day.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，賻祭如常儀。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor; condolence gifts and sacrifices followed the usual rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Grand Preceptor, and the usual rites of condolence were observed.

sentences.zh: 淮南大將王韶欲自為留後，令將士推己知軍事，且欲大掠。

translations.literal: Wang Shao, a great general of Huainan, wished to make himself acting military governor, ordered the officers and soldiers to recommend him to manage military affairs, and also wished to plunder on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao, a senior Huainan general, sought to declare himself acting military governor. He had his troops nominate him to command and planned a general sack of the region.

sentences.zh: 韓滉遣使謂之曰：「汝敢為亂，吾即日全軍渡江誅汝矣！」

translations.literal: Han Huang sent an envoy to tell him: "If you dare raise disorder, this very day my entire army will cross the river and execute you!"
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang sent a messenger: "Raise rebellion and my entire army crosses the Yangtze this very day to destroy you!

sentences.zh: 韶等懼而讓。

translations.literal: Shao and the others, in fear, yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao and his followers, terrified, backed down.

sentences.zh: 上聞之喜，謂李泌曰：「滉不惟安江東，又能安淮南，真大臣之器，卿可謂知人！」

translations.literal: The emperor, hearing this, was pleased and said to Li Mi: "Huang not only pacifies the lands east of the Jiang—he can also pacify Huainan. Truly the capacity of a great minister—you may be said to know men!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted. He told Li Mi: "Han Huang not only pacifies the Jiangdong region—he has secured Huainan as well. That is the mark of a true statesman. You knew the man well!

sentences.zh: 庚辰，加滉平章事，江淮轉運使。

translations.literal: On gengchen he was additionally made Regular Attendant-in-Chief and Jiang-Huai transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day Han Huang was made chief minister and commissioner for Jiang-Huai grain transport.

sentences.zh: 滉運江、淮粟帛入貢府，無虛月，韓廷賴之，使者勞問相繼，恩遇始深矣。

translations.literal: Huang transported Jiang-Huai grain and silks into the tribute storehouse without a single empty month; the Han court relied on this—the envoys bearing imperial greetings came one after another, and favor and treatment began to deepen.
translations.idiomatic: Month after month Han Huang shipped Jiang-Huai grain and silk to the capital without fail. The court depended on him; imperial envoys bearing commendations arrived in steady succession, and royal favor deepened.

sentences.zh: 是歲蝗遍遠近，草木無遺，惟不食稻，大饑，道殣相望。

translations.literal: That year locusts spread near and far; not a blade of grass or tree was left—they ate everything except rice. Great famine followed; corpses on the roads stared at one another.
translations.idiomatic: That year locusts ravaged the land, stripping every plant except rice. Famine followed. Corpses lined the roads as far as the eye could see.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝六貞元元年（

translations.literal: Sixth year, First year of Zhenyuan of Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial and Sagely Literate Emperor (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial and Sagely Literate — First year of Zhenyuan (

sentences.zh: 乙丑，公元七八五年）

translations.literal: yichou, AD 785)
translations.idiomatic: yichou, AD 785)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁酉朔，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on dingyou the new moon—amnesty for all under Heaven; the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of dingyou day, the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，贈顏真卿司徒，謚曰文忠。

translations.literal: On guichou Yan Zhenqing was posthumously granted Palace Secretary; his posthumous title was Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day Yan Zhenqing was posthumously ennobled as Palace Secretary with the posthumous title Wenzhong, "Cultured and Loyal."

sentences.zh: 新州司馬盧杞遇赦，移吉州長史，謂人曰：「吾必再入。」

translations.literal: Lu Qi, military adjutant of Xinzhou, benefited from the amnesty and was transferred to chief administrator of Jizhou. He told people: "I shall surely enter [office] again."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi, former military adjutant of Xinzhou, was pardoned and transferred to chief administrator of Jizhou. "I shall rise again," he told acquaintances.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上果用為饒州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor indeed employed him as prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor appointed him prefect of Raozhou, just as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 給事中袁高應草制，執以白盧翰、劉從一曰：「盧杞作相，致鑾輿播遷，海內瘡痍，奈何遽遷大郡！

translations.literal: Attendant Drafting-the-Draft Yuan Gao, who was to draft the edict, held it and informed Lu Han and Liu Congyi: "Lu Qi served as chief minister and caused the imperial carriage to wander in exile; within the seas wounds and scars abound—how can he suddenly be transferred to a great prefecture!
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Gao of the Secretariat, who was assigned to draft the appointment edict, brought the draft to Lu Han and Liu Congyi. "Lu Qi as chief minister drove the emperor into exile and left the realm in ruins," he said. "How can he be given a major prefecture so soon!

sentences.zh: 願相公執奏。」

translations.literal: I wish the chief ministers would firmly memorialize."
translations.idiomatic: I beg you, chief ministers, to memorialize against this.

sentences.zh: 翰等不從，更命它舍人草制。

translations.literal: Han and the others did not comply; another drafting attendant was ordered to compose the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Han and the others refused. Another drafting attendant was ordered to write the edict instead.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，製出，高執之不下，且奏：「杞極惡窮凶，百辟疾之若仇，六軍思食其肉，何可復用！」

translations.literal: On yimao the edict was issued; Gao held it and would not promulgate it, and moreover memorialized: "Qi is utterly wicked and utterly vicious—all the hundred officials hate him as an enemy; the six armies long to eat his flesh—how can he be employed again!"
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day the edict was issued. Yuan Gao refused to promulgate it and memorialized: "Lu Qi is utterly wicked. Every official in court hates him; every soldier in the army would gladly see him torn apart. He must not be restored!

sentences.zh: 上不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 補闕陳京、趙需等上疏曰：「杞三年擅權，百揆失敘，天地神祇所知，華夏、蠻夷同棄。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials Chen Jing, Zhao Xu, and others submitted memorials saying: "For three years Qi monopolized power; the hundred officials lost proper order—the gods of Heaven and Earth know it; Huaxia and the southern barbarians alike cast him off.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials Chen Jing, Zhao Xu, and others submitted memorials: "For three years Lu Qi wielded unchecked power and threw the bureaucracy into chaos. Heaven knows his crimes; Chinese and barbarian alike have cast him off.

sentences.zh: 倘加巨奸之寵，必失萬姓之心。」

translations.literal: If great favor is added to a great villain, the hearts of the myriad people will surely be lost."
translations.idiomatic: To honor so great a villain would forfeit the loyalty of the people.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，袁高復於正牙論奏。

translations.literal: On dingsi Yuan Gao again argued the matter before the main hall at court.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day Yuan Gao raised the matter again in open court.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「杞已再更赦。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Qi has already benefited from amnesty twice."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Lu Qi has already been pardoned twice.

sentences.zh: 高曰：「赦者止原其罪，不可為刺史。」

translations.literal: Gao said: "Amnesty only pardons the crime—it does not qualify one to serve as prefect."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Gao replied: "A pardon forgives the crime—it does not entitle a man to govern a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陳京等亦爭之不已，曰：「杞之執政，百官常如兵在其頸，今復用之，則奸黨皆唾掌而起。」

translations.literal: Chen Jing and the others also disputed without cease, saying: "Under Qi's administration the hundred officials were constantly as though soldiers were at their necks; if he is now employed again, then the villainous faction will all lick their palms and rise."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jing and the others pressed the argument relentlessly. "Under Lu Qi's rule every official lived with a blade at his throat," they said. "Restore him and every villain in the empire will stir.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，左右辟易，諫者稍引卻，京顧曰：「趙需等勿退，此國大事，當以死爭之。」

translations.literal: The emperor grew greatly angry; those at his sides scattered. The remonstrators gradually withdrew; Jing looked back and said: "Zhao Xu and the others—do not retreat! This is a great matter of state—we ought to dispute it unto death."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor erupted in fury. Attendants scattered. The remonstrators began to withdraw. Chen Jing called out: "Zhao Xu—do not leave! This is a matter of state. We must dispute it even at the cost of our lives.

sentences.zh: 上怒稍解。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger slightly eased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's rage subsided somewhat.

sentences.zh: 戊午，上謂宰相：「與杞小州刺史，可乎？」

translations.literal: On wuwu the emperor said to the chief ministers: "To give Qi a small prefecture—would that be acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day the emperor asked the chief ministers: "What if I appoint him to a small prefecture?

sentences.zh: 李勉曰：「陛下欲與之，雖大州亦可，其如天下失望何！」

translations.literal: Li Mian said: "If Your Majesty wishes to give it to him, even a great prefecture would be possible—but what of the disappointment of all under Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian replied: "If Your Majesty insists, even a great prefecture would be within your power—but think of the despair this would bring across the empire!

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以杞為澧州別駕。

translations.literal: On renxu Qi was made vice-prefect of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day Lu Qi was appointed vice-prefect of Lizhou—a minor post far from power.

sentences.zh: 使謂袁高曰：「朕徐思卿言，誠為至當。」

translations.literal: An envoy was sent to tell Yuan Gao: "I have slowly pondered your words—they are truly most apt."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent word to Yuan Gao: "I have reflected on what you said. You were entirely right.

sentences.zh: 又謂李泌曰：「朕已可袁高所奏。」

translations.literal: He also said to Li Mi: "I have approved what Yuan Gao memorialized."
translations.idiomatic: He told Li Mi as well: "I have accepted Yuan Gao's memorial.

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「累日外人竊議，比陛下於桓、靈；

translations.literal: Mi said: "For many days outsiders have privately discussed matters, comparing Your Majesty to Huan and Ling;
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi said: "For days now people have whispered, comparing Your Majesty to the corrupt emperors Huan and Ling of Han;

sentences.zh: 今承德音，乃堯、舜之不逮也！」

translations.literal: now, receiving Your virtuous pronouncement—this is what even Yao and Shun did not attain!"
translations.idiomatic: to hear Your Majesty's decision today—even Yao and Shun could not have done better!

sentences.zh: 上悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 杞竟卒於澧州。

translations.literal: Qi ultimately died at Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi died in exile at Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 高，恕己之孫也。

translations.literal: Gao was the grandson of Su Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Gao was the grandson of Su Ji.

sentences.zh: 三月，李希烈陷鄧州。

translations.literal: In the third month Li Xilie captured Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Li Xilie captured Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以汴滑節度使李澄為鄭滑節度使。

translations.literal: On wuwu Li Cheng, military governor of Bian-Hua, was made military governor of Zheng-Hua.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day Li Cheng, military governor of Bian-Hua, was transferred to govern Zheng-Hua.

sentences.zh: 以代宗女嘉誠公主妻田緒。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong's daughter, Princess Jiacheng, was given in marriage to Tian Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jiacheng, daughter of Emperor Daizong, was given in marriage to Tian Xu.

sentences.zh: 李懷光都虞候呂鳴岳密通款於馬燧，事洩，懷光殺之，屠其家。

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang's chief of army supervision Lu Mingyue secretly communicated his submission to Ma Sui; the matter leaked out. Huaiguang killed him and slaughtered his family.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Mingyue, chief of army supervision under Li Huaiguang, secretly offered his loyalty to Ma Sui. When the plot was discovered, Huaiguang executed him and slaughtered his entire family.

sentences.zh: 事連幕僚高郢、李鄘，懷光集將士而責之，郢、鄘抗言逆順，無所慚隱，懷光囚之。

translations.literal: The matter implicated staff members Gao Ying and Li Yong. Huaiguang assembled the officers and soldiers and reproached them. Ying and Yong spoke defiantly on right and wrong without shame or concealment; Huaiguang imprisoned them.
translations.idiomatic: The investigation implicated staff officers Gao Ying and Li Yong. Huaiguang assembled his officers and rebuked them. Gao and Li spoke boldly on loyalty and treason without evasion. Huaiguang had them imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 鄘，邕之侄孫也。

translations.literal: Yong was the grand-nephew of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong was the grand-nephew of the elder Li Yong.

sentences.zh: 馬燧軍於寶鼎，敗懷光兵於陶城，斬首萬餘級，分兵會渾瑊，逼河中。

translations.literal: Ma Sui encamped at Baoding, defeated Huaiguang's troops at Taocheng, beheaded more than ten thousand, divided his forces to join Hun Jian, and pressed upon Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui encamped at Baoding and routed Li Huaiguang's army at Taocheng, taking more than ten thousand heads. He then split his forces to join Hun Jian and pressed the siege toward Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁丑，以曹王皋為荊南節度，李希烈將李思登以隨州降之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on dingchou Cao Wang Gao was made military governor of Jingnan; Li Xilie's general Li Sideng surrendered Suizhou to him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dingchou day Prince Cao Li Gao was appointed military governor of Jingnan. Li Sideng, a general under Li Xilie, surrendered Suizhou to him.

sentences.zh: 壬午，馬燧、渾瑊破李懷光兵於長春宮南，遂掘塹圍宮城。

translations.literal: On renwu Ma Sui and Hun Jian defeated Li Huaiguang's troops south of Changchun Palace, then dug trenches and besieged the palace city.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day Ma Sui and Hun Jian routed Li Huaiguang's forces south of Changchun Palace, then dug trenches and encircled the palace compound.

sentences.zh: 懷光諸將相繼來降。

translations.literal: Huaiguang's generals came to surrender one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang's generals surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 詔以燧、瑊為招扶使。

translations.literal: An edict made Sui and Jian commissioners for summoning and comforting.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Ma Sui and Hun Jian commissioners for receiving surrenders.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙申，劉洽更名玄佐。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on bingshen Liu Qia changed his name to Xuanzuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingshen day, Liu Qia changed his name to Xuanzuo.

sentences.zh: 韓游瑰請兵於渾瑊，共取朝邑。

translations.literal: Han Yougui requested troops from Hun Jian to jointly take Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui asked Hun Jian for reinforcements to jointly capture Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 李懷光將閻晏欲爭之，士卒指邠軍曰：「彼非吾父兄，則吾子弟，奈何以白刃相向乎！」

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang's general Yan Yan wished to contest it; the soldiers pointed at the Bin army and said: "Those are not our fathers and elder brothers—they are our younger brothers and sons. How can we turn bare blades against one another!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang's general Yan Yan moved to oppose them. The soldiers pointed at Han Yougui's Binzhou troops and cried: "Those men are our fathers, brothers, and sons! How can we turn our blades on them!

sentences.zh: 語甚囂。

translations.literal: Their words were very clamorous.
translations.idiomatic: The outcry was fierce.

sentences.zh: 晏遽引兵去。

translations.literal: Yan at once withdrew his troops and left.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yan immediately withdrew his troops.

sentences.zh: 懷光知眾心不從，乃詐稱欲歸國，聚貨財，飾車馬，運俟路通入貢，由是得復逾旬月。

translations.literal: Huaiguang knew the people's hearts would not follow; he then falsely claimed he wished to return to allegiance, gathered goods and wealth, adorned carriages and horses, and transported them awaiting the road being open to enter tribute—by this he gained another full month and more.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that his army would not fight, Huaiguang feigned a desire to submit. He stockpiled wealth, decked out horses and carriages, and pretended to be preparing tribute for the emperor—buying himself another month and more of delay.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛巳，以劉玄佐兼汴州刺史。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on xinsi Liu Xuanzuo was additionally made prefect of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinsi day, Liu Xuanzuo was additionally appointed prefect of Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以金吾大將軍韋皋為西川節度使。

translations.literal: On xinmao Wei Gao, Grand General of the Golden Guard, was made military governor of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day Wei Gao, Grand General of the Golden Guard, was appointed military governor of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 朱滔病死，將士奉前涿州刺史劉怦知軍事。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao died of illness; the officers and soldiers installed the former prefect of Zhuo Liu Ping to manage military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao died of illness. His officers installed Liu Ping, former prefect of Zhuo, as acting commander.

sentences.zh: 時連年旱、蝗，度支資糧匱竭，言事者多請赦李懷光。

translations.literal: At the time drought and locusts continued for years; the treasury's grain stores were exhausted; many who spoke on affairs requested amnesty for Li Huaiguang.
translations.idiomatic: Years of drought and locusts had drained the treasury. Many at court urged the emperor to pardon Li Huaiguang.

sentences.zh: 李晟上言：「赦懷光有五不可：河中距長安才三百里，同州當其衝，多兵則未為示信，少兵則不足提防，忽驚東偏，何以制之！

translations.literal: Li Sheng submitted a memorial: "To amnesty Huaiguang has five impossibilities: Hezhong is only three hundred li from Chang'an; Tongzhou lies in its path—many troops and it is not showing trust; few troops and it is insufficient for defense; suddenly alarm the eastern flank—how can it be controlled!
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng memorialized: "There are five reasons not to pardon Li Huaiguang. Hezhong lies only three hundred li from Chang'an, with Tongzhou directly in its path. Station many troops there and we show no trust; station few and we cannot defend. If the eastern frontier is suddenly threatened, how do we respond? That is the first reason.

sentences.zh: 一也；

translations.literal: The first;
translations.idiomatic: First;

sentences.zh: 今赦懷光，必以晉、絳、慈、隰還之，渾瑊既無所詣，康日知又應遷移，土宇不安，何以獎勵，二也；

translations.literal: now, if Huaiguang is amnestied, Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi must be returned to him; Hun Jian would then have nowhere to go, Kang Rizhi would also have to be moved—territory and realm unsettled, how can there be reward and encouragement—the second;
translations.idiomatic: Second: pardon him and we must return Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi to his control. Hun Jian would have nowhere to go; Kang Rizhi would have to be relocated as well. With territories in flux, how do we reward loyalty?

sentences.zh: 陛下連兵一年，討除小丑，兵力未窮，遽赦其反逆之罪；

translations.literal: Your Majesty has wielded troops for a year, suppressing and eliminating a petty villain; military strength is not yet exhausted—suddenly to amnesty his crime of rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Third: Your Majesty has campaigned for a year to crush this rebel. Our strength is nowhere near spent—yet we would suddenly forgive treason.

sentences.zh: 今西有吐蕃，北有回紇，南有淮西，皆觀我強弱，不謂陛下施德澤，愛黎元，乃謂兵屈於人而自罷耳，必競起窺覦之心。

translations.literal: now to the west there is Tubo, to the north the Uyghurs, to the south Huai-Xi—all observe our strength and weakness; they will not say Your Majesty bestows virtue and favor and loves the black-haired people—they will say military force bowed before others and dismissed itself of its own accord; they will surely compete to rise with covetous hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: Tibet watches from the west, the Uyghurs from the north, Huai-Xi from the south. They weigh our strength. They will not believe Your Majesty acts from mercy—they will read it as weakness, that our armies were beaten and withdrew of their own accord. Every enemy at our borders will reach for ambition.

sentences.zh: 三也；

translations.literal: The third;
translations.idiomatic: Third;

sentences.zh: 懷光既赦，則朔方將士皆應敘勳行賞，今府庫方虛，賞不滿望，是愈激之使叛，四也；

translations.literal: once Huaiguang is amnestied, then the Shuofang officers and soldiers all ought to have merit recorded and rewards granted; now the treasury is just depleted—rewards will not satisfy their hopes; this would only further incite them to rebel—the fourth;
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: pardon Huaiguang and every Shuofang soldier will expect merit pay and rewards. The treasury is empty. Shortchanged men rebel all the more readily.

sentences.zh: 既解河中，罷諸道兵，賞典不舉，怨言必起，五也。

translations.literal: once Hezhong is relieved, the armies of the various circuits are dismissed, the reward rites are not performed—complaints will surely arise—the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: lift the siege of Hezhong, send the allied armies home, and fail to honor the promised rewards—and muttering will turn to open grievance.

sentences.zh: 今河中斗米五百，芻蒿且盡，牆壁之間，餓殍甚眾。

translations.literal: now in Hezhong a dou of rice costs five hundred; fodder and fuel are nearly exhausted; between the walls, the starved dead are very many.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong already pays five hundred cash for a dou of rice. Fodder and fuel are nearly gone. Between the city walls, the dead of hunger lie thick.

sentences.zh: 且其軍中大將殺戮略盡，陛下敕諸道圍守旬時，彼必有內潰之變，何必養腹心之疾，為他日之悔哉！」

translations.literal: moreover, the great generals in his army have been killed off almost entirely; if Your Majesty orders the various circuits to besiege and hold for ten days or so, they will surely have an internal collapse; why must you nourish a disease of the heart and belly, to become regret on some later day!"
translations.idiomatic: His senior commanders have slaughtered one another until almost none remain. Hold the siege another ten days and the camp will tear itself apart from within. Why keep a poison at your vitals only to rue it later?

sentences.zh: 又請發兵二萬，自備資糧，獨討懷光。

translations.literal: He also requested to raise twenty thousand troops, supply his own provisions, and alone attack Huaiguang.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to lead twenty thousand men at his own expense and finish Huaiguang himself.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲午朔，馬燧自行營入朝，奏稱：「懷光凶逆尤甚，赦之無以令天下，願更得一月糧，必為陛下平之。」

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day of the month jiawu, Ma Sui entered court from his field headquarters and memorialized: "Huaiguang's vicious rebellion is especially grave; to amnesty him is to have no way to command the realm. I wish to receive one more month's grain—I will surely pacify him for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the first day (jiawu), Ma Sui came to court from camp and memorialized: "Huaiguang's treason is too brazen for pardon; amnesty would cost you the realm's respect. Give me one month's rations and I will settle him for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 陝虢都知兵馬使達奚抱暉鴆殺節度使張勸，代總軍務，邀求旌節，且陰召李懷光將達奚小俊為援。

translations.literal: Daxi Baohui, Shan-Guo chief army-and-horse commissioner, poisoned military commissioner Zhang Quan, took charge of military affairs in his stead, demanded the commander's banner and credentials, and secretly summoned Li Huaiguang's general Daxi Xiaojun as aid.
translations.idiomatic: Daxi Baohui, chief army commissioner of Shan-Guo, poisoned Military Commissioner Zhang Quan, seized command of the army, demanded his own commissioner's banner and credentials, and secretly called in Li Huaiguang's general Daxi Xiaojun for support.

sentences.zh: 上謂李泌曰：「若蒲、陝連衡，則猝不可制。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Li Mi: "If Pu and Shan join forces, they cannot suddenly be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Li Mi: "If Huaiguang at Pu and Baohui at Shan join forces, we will lose control in an instant.

sentences.zh: 且抱暉據陝，則水陸之運皆絕矣。

translations.literal: moreover, if Baohui holds Shan, then transport by water and land will all be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: With Baohui holding Shanzhou, every water and land route for supplies will be severed.

sentences.zh: 不得不煩卿一往。」

translations.literal: I must trouble you to go once."
translations.idiomatic: I have no choice but to ask you to go yourself.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以泌為陝虢都防禦水陸運使。

translations.literal: On xinchou day Mi was made Shan-Guo chief defender and commissioner for water-and-land transport.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day the emperor appointed Mi chief defender of Shan-Guo and commissioner for water-and-land transport.

sentences.zh: 上欲以神策軍送泌之官，問「須幾何人？」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to have the Shence Army escort Mi to his post and asked, "How many men are needed?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted the Shence Army to escort Mi to his post and asked, "How many men do you need?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陝城三面懸絕，攻之未可以歲月下也，臣請以單騎入之。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Shan city hangs sheer on three sides; to assault it cannot be done within the span of months and years. Your servant asks to enter it alone on horseback."
translations.idiomatic: Mi replied: "Shanzhou's walls drop away on three sides. A siege would take more than a year. Let me ride in alone.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「單騎如何可入？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How can one enter alone on horseback?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "How can you enter alone?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陝城之人，不貫逆命，此特抱暉為惡耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "The people of Shan city are not accustomed to defying orders; this is simply Baohui doing evil.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "The people of Shan are not rebels by nature. Only Baohui is the villain here.

sentences.zh: 若以大兵臨之，彼閉壁定矣。

translations.literal: If a great army presses upon them, they will surely shut the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Send a large army and they will bar the gates at once.

sentences.zh: 臣今單騎抵其近郊，彼舉在兵則非敵，若遣小校來殺臣，未必不更為臣用也。

translations.literal: If your servant now goes alone on horseback to their near suburbs, if they mobilize all their troops they still cannot match me; if they send a petty officer to kill me, he may well instead be turned to my use.
translations.idiomatic: If I ride alone to their outskirts, their whole garrison cannot stop me. And if Baohui sends some low officer to cut me down, that man may yet serve me instead.

sentences.zh: 且今河東全軍屯安邑，馬燧入朝，願敕燧與臣同辭皆行，使陝人欲加害於臣，則畏河東移軍討之，此亦一勢也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, now the whole Hedong army is encamped at Anyi and Ma Sui has entered court; I wish Your Majesty would order Sui and me to take leave and depart together, so that if the people of Shan wish to harm me, they will fear the Hedong army shifting to attack them—this too is a kind of leverage."
translations.idiomatic: The entire Hedong army is at Anyi, and Ma Sui has just come to court. Order him and me to take leave and depart together. Anyone in Shan who thinks of harming me will fear Hedong marching against them. That too is leverage.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「雖然，朕方大用卿，寧失陝州，不可失卿，當更使他人往耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Even so, I am just now making great use of you. Better to lose Shan Prefecture than to lose you—I should send someone else instead."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Even so, I mean to rely on you heavily. I would rather lose Shanzhou than lose you. I ought to send someone else.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「他人必不能入。

translations.literal: He replied: "Another man certainly cannot enter.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "No one else can get in.

sentences.zh: 今事變之初，眾心未定，故可出其不意，奪其奸謀。

translations.literal: Now at the beginning of the upheaval, the hearts of the multitude are not yet settled; therefore one can strike by surprise and seize their treacherous plot.
translations.idiomatic: The crisis is fresh and minds are still unsettled. That is when surprise can break their conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 他人猶豫遷延，彼既成謀，則不得前矣。」

translations.literal: Another man would hesitate and delay; once they have completed their plot, one cannot advance."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone else would hesitate. Once their plans harden, no envoy will pass the gates.

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 泌見陝州進奏官及將吏在長安者，語之曰：「主上以陝、虢饑，故不授泌節而領運使，欲令督江、淮米以賑之耳。

translations.literal: Mi saw the Shan Prefecture memorial envoy and the officers and officials who were in Chang'an and said to them: "The sovereign, because Shan and Guo suffer famine, therefore did not grant Mi a commissioner's banner but put him in charge as transport commissioner, wishing to have him supervise Jiang and Huai grain to relieve them—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Mi sought out Shanzhou's memorial envoy and every officer from the circuit then in Chang'an and told them: "His Majesty knows Shan and Guo are starving. That is why he gave me no commissioner's banner, only the transport post—to bring Jiang-Huai grain and feed the people.

sentences.zh: 陝州行營在夏縣，若抱暉可用，當使將之。

translations.literal: The Shan Prefecture field headquarters is at Xia County; if Baohui can be used, he should be made to lead it.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanzhou field headquarters is at Xia County. If Baohui proves useful, he should command it.

sentences.zh: 有功，則賜旌節矣。」

translations.literal: If there is merit, then the banner and credentials will be granted."
translations.idiomatic: Serve well, and he will receive his commissioner's banner and credentials.

sentences.zh: 抱暉覘者馳告之，抱暉稍自安。

translations.literal: Baohui's scouts galloped to report this; Baohui grew somewhat reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Baohui's spies raced the news to him, and he began to relax.

sentences.zh: 泌具以語白上曰：「欲使其士卒思米，抱暉思節，必不害臣矣。」

translations.literal: Mi fully reported these words to the emperor and said: "I wish to make his soldiers think of grain and Baohui think of the commissioner's banner—he will surely not harm me."
translations.idiomatic: Mi told the emperor the whole plan: "Let the troops hunger for grain and Baohui hunger for a commission. Then he will not dare harm me.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 戊申，泌與馬燧俱辭行。

translations.literal: On wushen day Mi and Ma Sui both took leave to depart.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day Mi and Ma Sui both took formal leave and set out.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，加泌陝虢觀察使。

translations.literal: On gengxu day Mi was additionally made Shan-Guo observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day Mi was further appointed observation commissioner of Shan-Guo.

sentences.zh: 泌出潼關，鄜坊節度使唐朝臣以步騎三千佈於關外，曰：「奉密詔送公至陝。」

translations.literal: Mi passed out of Tong Pass; Yanfang military commissioner Tang Chaochen deployed three thousand infantry and cavalry outside the pass and said: "I obey a secret edict to escort you, sir, to Shan."
translations.idiomatic: Mi crossed Tong Pass. Yanfang Commissioner Tang Chaochen drew up three thousand foot and horse outside the gate and said, "By secret edict I am to escort you to Shan.

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「辭日奉進止，以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Mi said: "On the day I took leave I was told to await your orders and act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "When I took leave His Majesty told me to use my own judgment.

sentences.zh: 此一人不可相躡而來，來則吾不得入陝矣。」

translations.literal: This one man cannot follow close on my heels; if he comes, then I cannot enter Shan."
translations.idiomatic: Not one man may follow on my heels. If they do, I will never enter Shan.

sentences.zh: 唐臣以受詔不敢去，泌寫宣以卻之，因疾驅而前。

translations.literal: Tang Chaochen, having received the edict, dared not leave; Mi wrote out an imperial rescript to send him back, then spurred hard and pressed forward.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Chaochen, bound by his orders, would not withdraw. Mi wrote out a rescript turning him back and galloped on alone.

sentences.zh: 抱暉不使將佐出迎，惟偵者相繼。

translations.literal: Baohui did not let his generals and aides come out to welcome him; only scouts followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Baohui kept his officers inside and sent only a chain of scouts.

sentences.zh: 沁宿曲沃，將佐不俟抱暉之命來迎，泌笑曰：「吾事濟矣！」

translations.literal: Mi lodged at Quwo; generals and aides came to welcome him without waiting for Baohui's order. Mi laughed and said: "My affair is accomplished!"
translations.idiomatic: Mi stopped at Quwo. Officers came out to meet him without waiting for Baohui's word. Mi laughed: "It is done!

sentences.zh: 去城十五里，抱暉亦出謁。

translations.literal: Fifteen li from the city, Baohui also came out to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen li from the city Baohui came out to greet him in person.

sentences.zh: 泌稱其攝事保完城隍之功，曰：「軍中煩言，不足介意。

translations.literal: Mi praised his merit in holding affairs and preserving the city walls intact, and said: "Restless talk in the army is not worth minding.
translations.idiomatic: Mi praised him for keeping order and the walls intact, then said: "Pay no heed to the muttering in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 公等職事皆按堵如故。」

translations.literal: Your duties and posts all remain undisturbed as before."
translations.idiomatic: Every one of you keeps his post and duties unchanged.

sentences.zh: 抱暉出而喜。

translations.literal: Baohui went out rejoicing.
translations.idiomatic: Baohui withdrew delighted.

sentences.zh: 泌既入城視事，賓佐有請屏人白事者。

translations.literal: Once Mi had entered the city and assumed office, a guest-aide asked to dismiss the others and report a matter in private.
translations.idiomatic: After Mi entered the city and took up his duties, an aide asked to speak with the room cleared.

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「易帥之際，軍中煩言，乃其常理，泌到，自妥貼矣，不願聞也。」

translations.literal: Mi said: "At the moment of changing commanders, restless talk in the army is its ordinary rule; once Mi arrives, things settle of themselves—I do not wish to hear it."
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "Restless talk always follows a change of command. Now that I am here, order will settle of itself. I do not wish to hear it.

sentences.zh: 由是反仄者皆自安。

translations.literal: Thereupon those who had been uneasy all reassured themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At that every restless soul in the garrison calmed down.

sentences.zh: 泌但索簿書，治糧儲。

translations.literal: Mi only demanded the ledgers and set grain stores in order.
translations.idiomatic: Mi asked only for the account books and set about organizing the granaries.

sentences.zh: 明日，召抱暉至宅，語之曰：「吾非愛汝而不誅，恐自今有危疑之地，朝廷所命將帥皆不能入，故丐汝餘生，汝為我繼版、幣祭前使，慎無入關，自擇安處，潛來取家，保無它也。」

translations.literal: The next day he summoned Baohui to his residence and said to him: "It is not that I love you and will not execute you—I fear that from now on wherever there is peril and doubt, every commander the court appoints will be unable to enter; therefore I beg you your remaining life. Perform for me the ritual tablet and silk offering to mourn the former commissioner. Take care not to enter the pass. Choose your own safe place, come secretly to fetch your family—I guarantee you no other harm."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he summoned Baohui home and said: "This is not mercy—I spare you because any place under suspicion will shut its gates to the next man the court sends. Take your life and go. Perform the tablet-and-silk rites for the murdered commissioner. Do not cross back through the pass. Choose somewhere safe, slip back for your family, and you will come to no further harm.

sentences.zh: 泌之辭行也，上籍陝將預於亂者七十五人授泌，使誅之。

translations.literal: When Mi took leave to depart, the emperor registered seventy-five Shan generals implicated in the upheaval and handed the list to Mi, ordering their execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi had set out, the emperor gave him a roster of seventy-five Shan officers marked for the rebellion and ordered their deaths.

sentences.zh: 泌既遣抱暉，日中，宣慰使至。

translations.literal: Once Mi had sent Baohui away, at midday the pacification envoy arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Mi had already sent Baohui off when, at noon, the court's pacification envoy arrived.

sentences.zh: 泌奏「已遣抱暉，餘不足問。」

translations.literal: Mi memorialized: "Baohui has already been sent away; the rest are not worth inquiring into."
translations.idiomatic: Mi reported: "Baohui is already gone. The rest do not merit pursuit.

sentences.zh: 上復遣中使詣陝，必使誅之。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent a palace envoy to Shan, insisting that they be executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent another palace envoy to Shan and insisted on executions.

sentences.zh: 泌不得已，械兵馬使林滔等五人送京帥，懇請赦之。

translations.literal: Mi had no choice; he shackled army-and-horse commissioner Lin Tao and four others and sent them to the capital for execution, earnestly requesting their pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Mi had no choice. He fettered Army Commissioner Lin Tao and four others and sent them to the capital for execution, pleading earnestly for their lives.

sentences.zh: 詔謫戍天德；

translations.literal: An edict banished them to garrison duty at Tiande;
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent them into exile garrison at Tiande.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，竟殺之。

translations.literal: after more than a year, they were executed in the end.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later they were killed after all.

sentences.zh: 而抱暉遂亡命，不知所這。

translations.literal: Baohui then fled for his life; no one knew where he had gone.
translations.idiomatic: Baohui fled into hiding; no one knew where he went.

sentences.zh: 達奚小俊引兵至境，聞泌已入陝而還。

translations.literal: Daxi Xiaojun led troops to the border; hearing that Mi had already entered Shan, he turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Daxi Xiaojun marched to the border with relief troops, but turned back when he learned Mi was already inside Shan.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以劉怦為幽州、盧龍節度使。

translations.literal: On renzi day Liu Ping was made military commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day Liu Ping was appointed military commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong.

sentences.zh: 大旱，灞、滻將竭，長安井皆無水。

translations.literal: Great drought; the Ba and Chan rivers were nearly exhausted; every well in Chang'an had no water.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought nearly dried up the Ba and Chan rivers. Every well in Chang'an ran dry.

sentences.zh: 度支奏中外經費才支七旬。

translations.literal: The treasury office memorialized that expenses at court and in the provinces would last only seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury reported that court and provincial funds would last only seventy days.
